the king 's gambit is a chess opening that begins with the moves : white offers a pawn to divert the black e-pawn . if black accepts the gambit , white has two main plans . the first is to play d4 and bxf4 , regaining the gam bit pawn with central domination . the alternative plan is to Play nf3 and bc4 followed by 0-0 , when the semi-open f-file created after a pawn push to g3 allows white to attack the weakest point in black 's position , the pawn on f7 . theory has shown that , in order to maintain the gamb pawn , black may well be forced to weaken the with moves such as ... g5 or odd piece placement ( e.g . ) . a downside to the king 'S gambit, is that white weakens their own king ''s position , exposing it to the latent threat of ... qh4+ ( or ) . with a black pawn on c4 , white can not usually respond to the check with g3 , but if the king is forced to move then it also loses the right to castle.the King 's Gambit is one of the oldest documented openings . it was examined by the 17th-century italian chess player giulio cesare polerio , and also appears in one of its earliest chess books , luis ramírez de lucena 's `` repetición de amores y arte de ajedrez '' ( 1497 ) . the king ’s gamgame was one of many popular openings until the late 19th century , when improvements in defensive technique led it to decline in popularity . it is infrequently seen at master level today , as black has several methods to gain , but is still popular at amateur level .

a hedgehog is any of the spiny mammals of the subfamily erinaceinae , in the eulipotyphlan family erinacidae . there are seventeen species of hedgehog in five genera found through parts of europe , asia , and africa , and in new zealand by introduction .there are no hedgehogs native to australia and no living species native to the americas ( the extinct genus `` amphechinus '' was once present in north america ) .hedgehogs share distant ancestry with shrews ( family soricidae ) , with gymnures possibly being the intermediate link , and they have changed little over the last 15 million years . like many of the first mammals , they have adapted to a nocturnal way of life . their spiny protection resembles that of the unrelated porcupines , which are rodents , and echidnas , a type of monotreme .

on july 15 , 2020 , between 20:00 and 22:00 utc , reportedly 130 high-profile twitter accounts were compromised by outside parties to promote a bitcoin scam . twitter and other media sources confirmed that the perpetrators had gained access to twitter 's administrative tools so that they could alter the accounts themselves and post the tweets directly . they appeared to have used social engineering to gain access to the tools via twitter employees . three individuals were arrested by authorities on july 31 , 2020 and charged with wire fraud , money laundering , identity theft , and unauthorized computer access related to the scam.the scam tweets asked individuals to send bitcoin currency to a specific cryptocurrency wallet , with the promise of the twitter user that money sent would be doubled and returned as a charitable gesture . within minutes from the initial tweets , more than 320 transactions had already taken place on one of the wallet addresses , and bitcoin to a value of more than had been deposited in one account before the scam messages were removed by twitter . in addition , full message history data from eight non-verified accounts was also acquired.dmitri alperovitch , the co-founder of cybersecurity company crowdstrike , described the incident as `` the worst hack of a major social media platform yet . '' the federal bureau of investigation ( fbi ) and other law enforcement agencies are investigating the scam and the security used by twitter. security researchers expressed concerns that the social engineering used to execute the hack can affect the use of social media in important online discussions , including the lead-up into the 2020 united states presidential election .in addition , a number of other security researchers have also expressed concerns about the impact of the hack on the social media community.

uzlomac is a long mountain in bosnia and herzegovina ( bosnia ) , east from line direction maslovare – vrbanjci – kotor varoš – čelinac . it stretches from the southeast to the northwest through the mountainous area , from kruševica river ( west of borja mountains ) to jošavka . its maximum altitude is .the mountain is very rich in mixed forests resources and hunting wildlife , including bosnian endemic quarry mammals . its forest wealth is diverse : deciduous oak and deciduously beech . it also is rich in water resources : springs , streams and rivers . on uzlomac many tributaries of vrbenja river , usora and ukrina rise , i.e . tributary of the bosnian confluences .

thixotropy is a time-dependent shear thinning property . certain gels or fluids that are thick or viscous under static conditions will flow ( become thinner , less viscous ) over time when shaken , agitated , shear-stressed , or otherwise stressed ( time dependent viscosity ) . they then take a fixed time to return to a more viscous state.some non-newtonian pseudoplastic fluids are thixotropic fluids , exhibiting a constant shear stress for a long time but becoming fluid when agitated . some non-nucleoplastic liquids show a vixotropic fluid state when agitated , such as ketchup , and are called solidified fluids .some other non-toxic fluids show a time,dependent change in viscosities ; the longer the fluid undergoes shearstress , the lower its viscosITY . a thixobe fluid is a fluid which takes a finite time to attain equilibrium viscosness when introduced to a steep change in shear rate . some thixotrop fluids return to their gel state almost instantly , such like ketchup . and are sometimes called pseudoplatal fluids . others such as yogurt take much longer and can become nearly solid . many gels and colloids are thIXotropic materials , exhibiting an unstable form at rest but becoming rigid when agitated • thixot entropy arises because particles or structured solutes require time to organize . an overview of thixota has been provided by mewis and wagner.some fluids are anti-thixotropic : constant sheAR stress for one or more hours causes an increase or even solidification . fluids which exhibit this property are generally called rheopectic . anti-therapidation fluids are less well documented than hydrophobic fluids .

a disposable ( also called disposable product ) is a product designed for a single use after which it is recycled or is disposed as solid waste . the term is also sometimes used for products that may last several months ( e.g . disposable air filters ) to distinguish from similar products that last indefinitely ( e..g . washable air filters , etc ) . the word `` disposables '' is not to be confused with the word ` consumables '' , which is widely used in the mechanical world . for example , welders consider welding rods , tips , nozzles , gas , etc . to be `` consumables'' , as they last only a certain amount of time before needing to be replaced . consumables are needed for a process to take place , such as inks for printing and welding rods for welding , while disposable products are products that can be thrown away after it becomes damaged or otherwise unuseful .

zalmoxes is an extinct genus of rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the maastrichtian of romania . the genus is known from specimens first named as the species `` mochlodon robustum '' in 1899 by franz nopcsa before being reclassified as `` rhabderdodon robustus '' by him in 1915 . in 1990 this name was corrected to `` lhabdodon- robustus'' by george olshevsky , and in 2003 the species was once more reclassified , this time as the type species zalmoxES robustus . `` zaloxes '' refers to the dacian deity zalmoyis , and `` robustus ' to the robustness of the remains . in 2003 another species was named , zalmuxes shqiperorum , named for the albanian name for albanians .

healesville sanctuary , formally known as the sir colin mackenzie sanctuary , is a zoo specialising in native australian animals . it is located at healesville in rural victoria , australia , and has a history of breeding native animals .it is one of only two places to have successfully bred a platypus , the other being sydney 's taronga zoo . it also assists with a breeding population of the endangered helmeted honeyeater.the zoo is set in a natural bushland environment where paths wind through different habitat areas showcasing wallabies , wombats , dingoes , kangaroos , and over 200 native bird varieties.guided tours , bird shows and information areas are available to visitors .

potsdam ( ) is the capital and largest city of the german federal state of brandenburg . it directly borders the German capital , berlin , and is part of the berlin/brandenburg metropolitan region . it is situated on the river havel some southwest of berlin 's city centre.potsdam was a residence of the prussian kings and the germ kaiser until 1918 . its planning embodied ideas of the age of enlightenment : through a careful balance of architecture and landscape , potsdam was intended as `` a picturesque , pastoral dream '' which would remind its residents of their relationship with nature and reason.the city lies in an area of interconnected lakes and is distinguished by a series of cultural landmarks , in particular the parks and palaces of sanssouci , the largest world heritage site in germany . the potsdam conference in 1945 was held at cecilienhof palace.babelsberg , in the south-eastern part of potsdam , was already by the 1930s the home of a major film production studio and it has enjoyed success as an important center of european film production since the fall of the nordic wall . the filmstudio babelsberg is the oldest large-scale film studio in the world.potdam developed into a centre of science and engineering in the 19th century . today , there are three public colleges , the universities , the university and the postgraduate college in potsdam .babelberg , a small village in the north-eustical part of pansdam , is already the largest city in the country and it is the home to a number of film production studios.

james albert smith leach ( born october 15 , 1942 ) is an american academic and former politician . he served as ninth chair of the national endowment for the humanities from 2009 to 2013 and was a member of the u.s. house of representatives from iowa ( 1977–2007 ) .leach was the john l. weinberg visiting professor of public and international affairs at the woodrow wilson school of princeton university . he also served as the interim director of the institute of politics at the john f. kennedy school of government at harvard university from september 17 , 2007 , when bill purcell was appointed permanent director.previously , leach served 30 years ( 1977 –2007 ) as a republican member of Congress , representing ( numbered as the 1st district from 1977 to 2003 ) and was the vice president of the senate committee on banking and financial services ( 1995–2001 ) . he was a senior member of congress , serving as the chairman of the house committee on finance and banking services ( 1994–2002 ) and chaired the committee on international relations , serving on the committee’s subcommittee on asian and pacific affairs ( 2001–2006 ) and he also founded and served as co-chair of the congressional humanities caucus . he lost his 2006 re-election bid to democrat dave loebsack . leach sponsored the 1999 gramm–leach–bliley act , a notable piece of banking legislation of the 20th century .

suseok ( 수석 ) , also called viewing stones or scholar 's stones , is the korean term for small naturally occurring or shaped rocks which are traditionally valued . such stones are similar to chinese gongshi and japanese suiseki . `` suseok '' can be any color . they vary widely in size and shape . in some cases they can be very large . in other cases they are much smaller . in others they can weigh hundreds of kilograms or much less than one kilogram . the term also refers to the stones which are placed in traditional korean gardens .

jealousy generally refers to the thoughts or feelings of insecurity , fear , and concern over a relative lack of possessions or safety.jealousness can consist of one or more emotions such as anger , resentment , inadequacy , helplessness or disgust . in its original meaning , `` jealousy '' is distinct from envy , though the two terms have popularly become synonymous in the english language , with `` jealousy'' now also taking on the definition originally used for envy alone. [ edit ]Jealousy is a typical experience in human relationships , and it has been observed in infants as young as five months . some researchers claim that jealousy is seen in all cultures and is a universal trait . however , others claim jealousy is a culture-specific emotion.[1] Jealousy can either be perceived as a series of particularly strong emotions and constructed as a universal human experience . psychologists have proposed several models to study the processes underlying jealousy and have identified factors that result in jealousy . sociologists have demonstrated that cultural beliefs and values play an important role in determining what triggers jealousy and what constitutes socially acceptable expressions of jealousy . biologists have identified mechanisms that may unconsciously influence the expression of jealousy.throughout history , artists have also explored the theme of jealousy in photographs , paintings , films , songs , plays , poems , and books , and theologians have offered religious views of jealousy based on the scriptures of their respective faiths .

red is the color at the end of the visible spectrum of light , next to orange and opposite violet . it has a dominant wavelength of approximately 625–740 nanometres . it is a primary color in the rgb color model and the cmyk color model , and is the complementary color of cyan . reds range from the brilliant yellow-tinged scarlet and vermillion to bluish-red crimson , and vary in shade from the pale red pink to the dark red burgundy.red pigment made from ochre was one of the first colors used in prehistoric art . the ancient egyptians and mayans colored their faces red in ceremonies ; roman generals had their bodies colored red to celebrate victories . it was also an important color in china , where it was used to color early pottery and later the gates and walls of palaces . in the renaissance , the brilliant red costumes for the nobility and wealthy were dyed with kermes and cochineal . the 19th century brought the introduction of the second synthetic red dyes , which replaced the traditional dyes . red also became the color of revolution ; soviet russia adopted a red flag following the bolshevik revolution in 1917 , later followed by china, vietnam , and other communist countries. since red is the colour of blood , it has historically been associated with sacrifice , danger , and courage . in modern surveys in europe and the united states show red is also the color most commonly associated with heat , activity , passion , sexuality , anger , love , and joy .red dyes [ edit ]red also became popular in india and many other asian countries it is the type of revolution . soviat russia adopt a red Flag following the Bolshevik Revolution in 1917 beginning followed by bina , vietnan , and various communist countries.[citation needed]since red is often associated with the color red , it tends to be associated with sacrifices , death , or courage . modern survey results in the europe region and the western states show that red is very popular with people of all ages . red is a color most frequently associated with warmth , activity . red can also symbolize happiness and good fortune .

typesetting is the composition of text by means of arranging physical types or the digital equivalents . stored letters and other symbols ( called sorts in mechanical systems and glyphs in digital systems ) are retrieved and ordered according to a language 's orthography for visual display . typesetting requires one or more fonts ( which are widely but erroneously confused with and substituted for typefaces ) . one significant effect of typesetting was that authorship of works could be spotted more easily , making it difficult for copiers who have not gained permission .

charles frederick `` karch '' kiraly ( ) ( born november 3 , 1960 ) is an american volleyball player , coach and broadcast announcer . in the 1980s he was a central part of the u.s national team that won gold medals at the 1984 and 1988 olympic games . he went on to win the gold medal again at the 1996 olympus games , the first olympo competition to feature beach volleyball . he is the only player ( man or woman ) to have won olympics gold medals in both the indoor and beach volleyball categories . he played college volleyball for the ucla bruins , where his teams won three national championships under head coach al scates.kiraly is currently the head coach of the united states women 's national volleyball team .

the glass frogs are frogs of the amphibian family centrolenidae ( order anura ) . while the general background coloration of most glass frogs is primarily lime green , the abdominal skin of some members of this family is transparent and translucent . the internal viscera , including the heart , liver , and gastrointestinal tract , are visible through the skin , hence the common name is given as glass frog . glass frog are arboreal , meaning they mainly live in trees , and only come out for mating season .

gliese 667 cc ( also known as gj 667cc , hr 6426cc , or hd 156384cc ) is an exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of the red dwarf star gliese six67 c , which is a member of the gliesa 667 triple star system , approximately 23.62 light-years ( 6.8 parsecs , or about 217,000,000,-000,0000 km ) away in the constellation of scorpius . the exoplanets was found by using the radial velocity method , from radial-velocity measurements via observation of doppler shifts in the spectrum of the planet 's parent star .

a leaf blower , commonly known as blower, is a gardening tool that propels air out of a nozzle to move debris such as leaves and grass cuttings . leaf blowers are powered by electric or gasoline motors . gasoline models have traditionally been two-stroke engines , but four-stroke generators were recently introduced to partially address air pollution concerns . leafblowers are typically self-contained handheld units , or backpack mounted units with a handheld wand . the latter is more ergonomic for prolonged use . larger units may rest on wheels and even use a motor for propulsion . these are sometimes called `` walk behind leaf blows '' because they must be pushed by hand to be operated.some units can also suck in leaves and small twigs via a vacuum , and shred them into a bag . in that role it is called a blower vac .

sheyi emmanuel adebayor ( ; born 26 february 1984 ) is a togolese professional footballer who plays as a striker . he previously played for english clubs arsenal , manchester city , tottenham hotspur and crystal palace , as well as french side metz , monégasque team monaco , spanish team real madrid , turkish clubs i̇stanbul başakşehir and kayserispor , and paraguay 's olimpia asunción.he was voted african footballer of the year for 2008 while playing at arsenal , and during his latter career , he became the most iconic signing in paraguayan football and the highest paid player in the country 's history.adebayor represented the togo national team at the 2006 fifa world cup in germany , the country's debut , and to date only , appearance at the world cup . in january 2010 , he was one of the players involved when the to go team 's bus came under gunfire on the way to the 2010 africa cup of nations in angola , after which he retired from national team duty . in 2013 , he returned to togo team for the 2013 african cup of nation in south africa , where he helped them to qualify for the quarter-finals . he is currently togo 's all-time top goalscorer with 32 goals . he made his first ever , appearances at the tournament . in juary 2010 beginning , adebbeyor was part of the drivers involved when it was reported that the squad was hit by a bus . in 2010 , adebayor was one member of the team on the road to the north africa . in 2011 , he retired due to injury . in 2012 , he went to play for the tobe team again in 2013 afrika cup of foods in south east africa where he contributed them to survive for the semi-finals and he is current togo "s all -time top goalcorerwith 32 goals."

bodcaw is a town in nevada county , arkansas , united states . the population was 154 at the 2000 census . it is part of the hope micropolitan statistical area .

an observation deck , observation platform , or viewing platform is an elevated sightseeing platform usually situated upon a tall architectural structure , such as a skyscraper or observation tower . observation decks are sometimes enclosed from weather , and a few may include coin-operated telescopes for viewing distant features .
william thomas hart ( born february 4 , 1929 ) is a former United States district judge of the united states district court for the northern district of illinois .

sportverein grödig is an austrian association football club from Grödig . the team currently competes in the austrian regional league west , the third tier of austrian football.grödig were relegated from the austria bundesliga at the end of the 2015–16 season ; however , they dropped down two levels to the austrians regional league east due to financial problems .

donn alan pennebaker ( ; july 15 , 1925 – august 1 , 2019 ) ( often credited as d.a . penne baker ) was an american documentary filmmaker and one of the pioneers of direct cinema . performing arts and politics were his primary subjects . in 2013 , the academy of motion picture arts and sciences recognized his body of work with an academy honorary award.pennebacher has been described as `` arguably the pre-eminent chronicler of sixties counterculture '' .

jiang yi-huah ( ; born 18 november 1960 ) is a taiwanese politician and former premier of the republic of china ( roc ) . on 29 noovember 2014 , he tendered his resignation and was succeeded by mao chi-kuo on 8 december 2014.prior to his appointment as the premier , jiang was the vice premier of China from 2012 to 2013 . he served as minister of the interior from 2009 to 2012 and minister of research , development and evaluation commission of the executive yuan from 2008 to 2009 .

voltage , electric potential difference , electric pressure or electric tension is the difference in electric potential between two points , which ( in a static electric field ) is defined as the work needed per unit of charge to move a test charge between the two points . in the international system of units , the derived unit for voltage ( potential difference ) is named `` volt '' . in si units , work per unit charge is expressed as joules per coulomb , where 1 volt = 1 joule ( of work ) per 1 coulom ( of charge ) . the old si definition for `` volt'' used power and current , since 1990 quantum hall and josephson effect were used and recently ( 2019 ) fundamental physical constants were introduced for the definition of all si units and derived units . voltage or electric potential differences is denoted symbolically by , simplified `` v '' , or `` u '' , for instance in the context of ohm 's or kirchhoff 's circuit laws.electric potential differences between points can be caused by electric charge , by electric current through a magnetic field , by time-varying magnetic fields , by some combination of these three . a voltmeter can be used to measure the voltage ( or potential difference ), electric pressure , electric tension , or electric pressure . a voltage meter may be used as a reference potential for a point in a system ; often a common reference potential such as the ground of the system is used as one of the points .a voltage may represent either a source of energy ( electromotive force ) or lost , used , or stored energy ( potential drop ) .

lars mortimer ( 22 march 1946 – 25 august 2014 ) was a swedish comic artist who wrote and illustrated , among many others , the swedISH comic strips `` bobo '' and `` hälge . `` mortimer died after a short illness on 25 augus 2014 in alfta , hälsingland . he was 68 .

a blast injury is a complex type of physical trauma resulting from direct or indirect exposure to an explosion . blast injuries occur with the detonation of high-order explosives as well as the deflagration of low order explosives . these injuries are compounded when the explosion occurs in a confined space .

jose c. vitug ( born 15 july 1934 ) is a filipino lawyer and jurist who served as an associate justice of the supreme court of the philippines . he was appointed to the court on june 28 , 1993 by president fidel ramos and retired on july 15 , 2004.vitug was the founding dean of the angeles university foundation school of law . he serves as an independent director aboitiz equity ventures .

the british rail class 304 electric multiple units were built for suburban use on the first phases of the west coast main line electrification between crewe and manchester/liverpool/rugby . originally classed as am4 units , they later became class 304 under the tops numbering system , and could be found in operation over most of the east coast main branch . the units conformed to the 1959-design for alternating current ( ac ) electrical multiple units , and were externally very similar to the class 305 , class 308 and the 1,200 v direct current ( dc ) class 504 units . no units survived into preservation , and all units were eventually scrapped .

major-general sir herbert benjamin edwardes ( 12 november 1819 – 23 december 1868 ) was a british administrator , soldier , and statesman active in the punjab region of north-east India . he is best known as the `` hero of multan '' for his pivotal role in securing britam victory in the second anglo-sikh war .

jean-michel larrasket ( , ) ( 22 may 1950 – 19 march 2018 ) , was a french professor and engineer , as well as vice president for the french basque country in the basque studies society . he was a promoter of several projects for the social and economic development of the french basinque country , and he was also one of the founders of the `` eticoop '' cooperative that promotes entrepreneurship in this geographical area .

ingram olkin ( july 23 , 1924 – april 28 , 2016 ) was a professor emeritus and chair of statistics and education at stanford university and the stanf graduate school of education . he is known for developing statistical analysis for evaluating policies , particularly in education , and for his contributions to meta-analysis , statistics education , multivariate analysis , and majorization theory .

ramo peter ( ray ) ceresino ( april 24 , 1929 – may 1 , 2015 ) was a canadian ice hockey left winger . he played for the toronto maple leafs of the nhl . on june 2 , 1953 , he married lorraine giardetti ; they were married for 62 years . he moved his family to california in 1962 and settled in los angeles where he worked as a mortgage broker . he later retired to san diego.he had three children , including gordon ceresinos .

pope gregory xvi ( ; born bartolomeo alberto cappellari ; 18 september 1765 – 1 june 1846 ) was head of the catholic church and ruler of the papal states from 2 february 1831 to his death in 1846 . he had adopted the name mauro upon entering the religious order of the camaldolese.strongly conservative and traditionalist , he opposed democratic and modernising reforms in the papial states and throughout europe , seeing them as fronts for revolutionary leftism . against these trends , gregORY xvi sought to strengthen the religious and political authority of the Papacy ( see ultramontanism ) . in the encyclical `` mirari vos '' , he pronounced it `` false and absurd , or rather mad , that we must secure and guarantee to each one liberty of conscience . '' he encouraged missionary activity abroad and condemned the slave trade . however , his harsh repression , financial extravagance and neglectfulness left him deeply unpopular domestically.he is the most recent pope to take the pontifical name `` gregories '' , and the most-recent non-bishop to become pope . he was , until the accession of pope francis in 2013 , the first pope to have been a priest of a religious order .

world music ( also called global music or international music ) is a western musical category encompassing many different styles of music from other parts of the globe . it includes many forms of music that westerners consider ethnic , indigenous music , folk music , neotraditional music , and music where more than one cultural tradition , such as non-western music and western popular music , intermingle.world music 's inclusive nature and elasticity as a musical category may pose some obstacles to a universal definition , but its ethic of interest in the culturally exotic is encapsulated in `` froots '' magazine 's description of the 'genre ' as `` local music from out there '' .the term was popularized in the 1980s as a marketing category for non-Western traditional music . it has grown to include subgenres such as ethnic fusion ( clannad , ry cooder , enya , etc . ) and worldbeat .

rameswaram ( also spelt as ramesvaram , rameshwaram ) is a town and municipality in the ramanathapuram district of the indian state of tamil nadu . it is on pamban island separated from mainland india by the pam ban channel and is about 40 kilometres from mannar island , sri lanka . it has a population of 44,856 as of 2011 . rameswaram is situated in the gulf of mannar , at the tip of the northern part of the island , and is located in the middle of the rama sethu . ramswaram island , also known as kachchatheevu , is the closest point from which to reach india , and it is located at the southern end of the ramayana , at a distance of about 50 kilometres from the port city of chennai . the town is the terminus of the railway line from chenna and madurai . together with varanasi , it is considered to be one of the holiest places in india to hindus , and part of its char dham pilgrimage.it is written in the Ramayana that the divine king rama built a bridge with hanuman 's help from here across the sea to lanka to rescue his wife sita from her abductor ravana . the ramerathaswamy temple , dedicated to the vedic god shiva , is at the centre of the town and is closely associated with rama . the temple and the town are considered a holy pilgrimage site for shaivas.rames waram is also known for its sethu , which was a former land connection between india and rama , and geological evidence suggests that the tamanathaswaram sethu was not a land connection from india . ramaswaram has been in the news over the sethusamudram shipping canal project , kachatheevuvu , sRI lankan tamil refugees and capturing local fishermen for alleged cross-border activities by sri jankan forces . ramewaram town is administered by a municipality established in 1994 .the town covers an area of and had a population Of 44, 856 asof 2011 . tourism and fishery employ the majority of workforce in rames waram .

plains is a town and the county seat of yoakum county of western texas , united states , particularly the south ( inner ) half of the panhandle 's plains . the city 's population was 1,481 at the 2010 census .

a consonant followed by a vowel like `` '' ka '' ''( か ) or `` '' n '' ( ん ) , a nasal sonorant which , depending on the context , sounds either like english `` m '' , `` n '' or `` ng '' ( ) when syllable-final or like the nasal vowels of french , portuguese or galician . because the characters of the kana do not represent single consonants ( except in the case of ん `` n'' ) , they are referred to as syllabic symbols and not alphabetic letters.The kana are used to write `` okurigana '' ( kana suffixes following a kanji root , for example to inflect verbs and adjectives ) , various grammatical and function words including particles , as well as miscellaneous other native words for which there are no kanji or whose kanji form is obscure or too formal for the writing purpose . words that do have common kanji renditions may also sometimes be written instead in hirsagana , according to an individual author 's preference , for examples to impart an informal feel . hirago is also used to provide `` okurtigana ' ( kanji suffixesFollowing a kanjū , a reading aid that shows the pronunciation of kanji characters ) , numerous grammatical, function words , various Grammatical and Function words including the kanji word , and various grammars , for a variety of other kanji forms is often written in kana , for the purposes of providing a formal feel. words that don’t usually have common kana renditions are also sometimes written in hiraganana , but may also be used to give a sense of the pronunciation or a reading aids that shows how to write them in kanji character. hIRagana is also known as kana ordering.there are two main systems of ordering hirgana : the old-fashioned iroha ordering and the more prevalent gojūon ordering .
san diego is a city in duval and jim wells counties , texas , united states . the population was 4,488 at the 2010 census . it is located primarily in duvin county , of which it is the county seat .

linux mint is a community-driven linux distribution based on ubuntu or debian . linux mint comes bundled with a variety of free and open-source applications and can provide full out-of-the-box multimedia support for those who choose ( by ticking one box as part of the installation process of the os ) to include some proprietary software , such as multimedia codecs.the project was created by clément lefèbvre and is being actively developed by the linux mint team and community .

our band could be your life : scenes from the american indie underground , 1981–1991 is a book by michael azerrad . it chronicles the careers of several underground rock bands who , while finding little or no mainstream success , were hugely influential in establishing american alternative and indie rock , mostly through nearly constant touring and records released on small , regional independent record labels , as well as major independent labels , and also conducted extensive research of old fanzines , magazines , and books .

everland is south korea 's largest theme park . located at the everland resort in yongin , a city in gyeonggi-do , it receives 5,85 million visitors annually and was ranked nineteenth in the world for amusement park attendance in 2018 . along with its main attractions , everland includes a zoo and water park known as caribbean bay . everland is operated by samsung c & t corporation ( formerly known as samsung everland , cheil industries ) , which is a subsidiary of the samsung group.this park was formerly called `` jayeon nongwon '' which roughly translates to `` natural farm . '' its former english name was `` farmland . '' this park is now known as `` iyongwon , '' and it has been renamed to `` iyo nongwan . ''

warendorf is a `` kreis '' ( district ) in the northern part of north rhine-westphalia , germany . neighboring districts are steinfurt , osnabrück ( district ), , gütersloh , soest , district-free city münster , coesfeld and the district-universität Münster .

frank cloud cooksey ( born june 3 , 1933 ) is an american public servant . he served as student body president of the university of texas in the 1950s . he worked as an attorney in the civil rights division of the u.s. district attorney , the texas attorney general 's office ( under john hill ) and in private practice . he was mayor of austin , texas from 1985 to 1988 . he is also an environmental activist , and is known for his progressive stance during his term as mayor .

metamorphic rocks arise from the transformation of existing rock types , in a process called metamorphism , which means `` change in form '' . the original rock ( protolith ) is subjected to heat ( temperatures greater than 150 to 200 °c ) and pressure ( or more ) , causing profound physical or chemical change . the protolith may be a sedimentary , igneous , or existing metamorphic rock.metamorphics make up a large part of the earth 's crust and form 12 % of the world 's land surface . they are classified by texture and by chemical and mineral assemblage ( metamorphica facies ) . they may be formed simply by being deep beneath the earth's surface , subjected to high temperatures and the great pressure of the rock layers above it . they can form from tectonic processes such as continental collisions , which cause horizontal pressure , friction and distortion .they are also formed when rock is heated by the intrusion of hot molten rock called magma from the earth's interior . the study of metamorphics ( now exposed at the earth ’s surface following erosion and uplift ) provides information about the temperatures and pressures that occur at great depths within the earth.'s crust.some examples of metabolic rocks are gneiss , slate , marble , schist , and quartzite .

nuclear espionage is the purposeful giving of state secrets regarding nuclear weapons to other states without authorization ( espionage ) . there have been many cases of known nuclear espionage throughout the history of nuclear weapons and many times of suspected or alleged espionage . because nuclear weapons are generally considered one of the most important of State secrets , all nations with nuclear weapons have strict restrictions against the giving of information relating to nuclear weapon design , stockpiles , delivery systems , and deployment . states are also limited in their ability to make public the information regarding nuclear weapon by non-proliferation agreements .

Magnús Eiríksson, born on June 22, 1806 in Skinnalón (Norður-Þingeyjarsýsla), Iceland, died on July 3, 1881 in Copenhagen, Denmark. He was an Icelandic theologian who criticized Søren Aabye Kierkegaard and Hans Lassen Martensen in Copenhagen. Eiríksson had a very critical view of church teachings, especially about the Trinity and Jesus being divine. Instead, he emphasized God's unity and saw Jesus mainly as a prophet and teacher. Because of his ideas, people called him a "pioneer" or "precursor" to Unitarianism in Denmark.

Brewer played for several teams during his career: the Islanders, Oilers, Blues, Lightning, Ducks, and Maple Leafs. He was also the captain of the Blues for two years. Brewer also played for the Prince George Cougars and Lowell Lock Monsters. In 1999, he was chosen for the Prince George Cougars' all-time team in a Canadian hockey league promotion. Brewer represented Canada eight times at international events. He won three ice hockey world championships gold medals and one World Cup of Hockey gold medal. His Olympic gold came from the 2002 Winter Olympics. For this, he was inducted into the BC Sports Hall of Fame with his teammates in 2003.

Yellowcake, also called urania, is a powdery form of uranium concentrate. It comes from solutions after processing uranium ores. Yellowcake is made after mining but before turning the uranium into fuel or enriching it further. The process to get yellowcake varies depending on the type of ore. First, the ore is ground and chemically treated. The result is a coarse powder that smells strong and doesn't dissolve in water. It contains about 80% uranium oxide, which melts at around 2880°C.

The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, or ANWR, is in northeastern Alaska. It covers part of the Alaska North Slope region. ANWR is the biggest national wildlife refuge in the United States. The office managing it is in Fairbanks. Many animals live there, like polar bears, grizzly bears, black bears, moose, caribou, wolves, eagles, lynx, wolverines, martens, beavers, and birds that migrate. Across the border in Canada are two national parks called Ivvavik and Vuntut.

The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) represents music companies in the United States. It includes record labels and distributors as members. The RIAA says these members make about 85% of all legally sold music in the U.S. Founded in 1952, its first job was to handle copyright fees, work with trade unions, and research record industry issues and government rules. Early standards set by the RIAA included how sound should be recorded on records, the format for stereo grooves, and the size of different types of records. Currently, the RIAA lobbies in the U.S., spends over $6 million each year. It also manages the rights to sound recordings collectively and certifies gold and platinum music albums and singles in the United States.

Happy Valley Shanghai is an amusement park in China. It is in Songjiang District and is not far from downtown Shanghai. The park covers a large area. It opened on August 16, 2009, making it the fourth Happy Valley theme park.

Stewart-Haas Racing is an American car race team. They compete in NASCAR Cup Series, Xfinity Series, K & N Pro West Series, and iRacing series. The team is co-owned by Tony Stewart, a three-time champion, and Gene Haas, who started Haas Automation. The team was formed in 2002 as Haas CNC Racing after Gene Haas decided to create his own team instead of continuing with Hendrick Motorsports. In 2009, Tony Stewart joined the team, getting a 50% stake in it by driving for them. Stewart-Haas Racing is based in Kannapolis, North Carolina, near Charlotte Motor Speedway. They have a sister team called Haas F1 racing but are separate legally. In NASCAR Cup Series, they use four Ford Mustang GT cars: No. 4 with Kevin Harvick, No. 10 with Aric Almirola, No. 14 with Clint Bowyer, and No. 41 with Cole Custer. In the Xfinity Series, they have one full-time Ford Mustang driven by Chase Briscoe. In K & N Pro West Series, they run one part-time Ford Mustang No. 41 with Aric Almirola. The Xfinity team works with Biagi-Denbeste Racing. From the start until 2016, Stewart-Haas used Chevrolet engines and chassis from Hendrick Motorsports (except for 2003 when they used Pontiac). In 2017, they switched to Ford engines, Roush Yates Engines, and started building their own chassis. They have won in all three major NASCAR national touring divisions, making them one of only a few teams to do so.

The Arc de Triomphe de l'Etoile is a famous monument in Paris, France. It's at the end of Champs-Élysées, in the center of Place Charles de Gaulle, which used to be called Place de l'Etoile—the "star" due to its twelve roads radiating from it. The monument stands between three parts of Paris: the 16th arrondissement (south and west), the 17th (north), and the 8th (east). It honors soldiers who fought for France in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, with their names on its surfaces. Beneath it lies a tomb for an unknown soldier from World War I. As part of Paris's "historic axis," a line of monuments and important streets leading to Grande Arche de la Défense, the Arc was designed by Jean Chalgrin in 1806. Sculptures on it show French youth against German warriors. Standing at about 50 meters tall and wide, with an inner vault nearly 30 meters high and 20 meters wide, it is a central landmark. In 1919, a pilot flew his plane through the arch as part of a victory parade after World War I ended. Before the Arc de Triomphe, Mexico City's Monumento a la Revolución was the tallest triumphal arch at about 65 meters high. Pyongyang’s Arch of Triumph is similar in design and slightly taller, while La Grande Arche near Paris is also very tall but not named an Arc de Triomphe.

Giuseppina Bozzacchi, born in Milan on November 23, 1853, was a young Italian dancer. At just 16 years old, she performed the role of Swanhilda in the ballet "Coppélia," created by Léo Delibes, for the Paris Opera Ballet. Bozzacchi had come to study dancing in Paris with Mme Dominique. Earlier, choreographer Arthur Saint-Léon and director Émile Perrin had been looking for someone to play Swanhilda but couldn't find a suitable dancer among those they considered, including Léontine Beaugrand and Angelina Fioretti. In 1868, the favorite ballerina of Saint-Léon was preparing for the role when she fell ill. In 1869, Saint-Léon and Perrin asked composer Léo Delibes to find a suitable Swanhilda on his trip to Italy. He didn't return with anyone but they found Bozzacchi, who performed the role of Swanhilda for the first time on May 25, 1870, in front of Emperor Napoleon III. Bozzacchi repeated her performance several times after that. However, in July, a war broke out between France and Prussia over Spain's throne. On July 19, France declared war. Bozzacchi danced Swanhilda for the last time on August 31, just before the Paris Opera closed due to the Franco-Prussian War. Due to the opera not paying salaries and a lack of food, Bozzacchi became weak and fell ill with smallpox and fever. She died in the morning of her 17th birthday and was buried at Cimetière de Montmartre in Paris.

By April 2013, over two million copies were sold worldwide. Dark Souls got two sequels in the middle of the 2010s, and a remade version came out in 2018.

Three 6 Mafia is an American hip hop group from Memphis, Tennessee, formed in 1991. They started as a horror-themed underground rap group and later became famous. Their first album, "Mystic Stylez," came out in 1995 and was very influential. The group released music with independent labels like Prophet Entertainment and their own label, Hypnotize Minds, as well as Relativity, Loud, and Columbia Records. Two of their albums were RIAA-certified platinum: "Dogg Food" (2000) and "Most Known Unknown" (2005). The song "Stay Fly" from the second album was a hit. In 2006, they won an Academy Award for best original song for "It's Hard Out Here for a Pimp," which is from the movie "Hustle & Flow." Their latest studio album, "Last 2 Walk," came out in 2008. As of 2016, their total worldwide album sales were 5.5 million.

Lewis Michael Eisenberg, born October 12, 1942, is an American financier and investor who became the United States Ambassador to Italy. He helped start a private investment company called Granite Capital International Group. He has been involved in American politics for many years and held important roles, such as being the chairman of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey during the 9/11 attacks. In July 2017, Donald Trump chose Eisenberg to be the new U.S. Ambassador to Italy. The Senate agreed on August 3, 2017.

The South African Republic, known as Transvaal, existed from 1852 to 1902. It was an independent country in what is now South Africa. This Republic won against the British Empire in a war called the First Boer War and stayed free until the end of the Second Boer War on May 31, 1902. After losing, many women and children living there died due to harsh conditions. Following this war, the area became part of the Transvaal Colony. During World War I, people tried to restart the Republic through an event called the Maritz Rebellion. Today, much of what used to be the South African Republic is now in parts of Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and North West provinces in northeastern South Africa.
Italy has taken part in every Military World Games event since 1995.

College Station is a city in Brazos County, Texas. It is located in east-central Texas, in an area known as the Brazos Valley, near the center of what's called the Texas Triangle. College Station is about 100 miles northwest of Houston and around 90 miles northeast of Austin. According to the 2010 census, College Station had a population of 93,857. By July 2019, that number grew to an estimated 117,911. College Station is part of a larger area with Bryan called the Bryan-College Station Metropolitan Area, which had 273,101 people in 2019. College Station is where Texas A&M University's main campus is located. This university helps give the city its name and existence because it was built along a railroad. As a land-, sea-, and space-grant institution, Texas A&M does lots of research that benefits College Station, with projects funded by groups like NASA and the National Institutes of Health. Because so many people in College Station have college degrees, "Money" magazine named it one of the most educated cities in Texas in 2006. It was also ranked as the 11th-most educated city in the United States that year.
Giornico is a town in the Leventina area, which is part of Ticino in Switzerland.
Jefferson County is a name used for 26 counties and one parish in the United States.
blingel is a small town in Pas-de-Calais, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France.

The Citadel Center is a tall building in Chicago, 580 feet (177 meters) high. It stands at 131 S. Dearborn St., Chicago, Illinois, 60603. A Spanish architect named Ricardo Bofill designed it. As of fall 2018, it was the 57th tallest building in Chicago and soon became the 60th tallest. The building was finished in 2003 and has 37 floors above ground and 3 below, making a total of 40 floors. It covers 1,536,548 square feet. In 2017, it received LEED Gold certification. In the past, there was a special sculpture in its lobby—a limited-edition copy of the Winged Victory of Samothrace. The original statue is at the Louvre Museum. The lobby also had walls made of reddish wood called padauk. The Citadel Center was the first building in Chicago to use a raised-floor pressurized plenum system, which allowed for better control of the climate by using adjustable floor diffusers.

Luke Isaac Moore was born on February 13, 1986. He played soccer professionally and was a striker. Moore also played for England's under-21 team. He has an older brother named Stefan who used to play professional soccer too.

Saint-Jean-sur-Evre was once its own small town in Mayenne, a part of France in the northwest. On January 1, 2017, Saint-Jean-sur-Evre joined with another town called Blandouet to become one new town.

Sound drowned, sometimes called Dis, is a UK music website funded by Silentway, an artist management company. The site was started by Sean Adams. It includes reviews, news, interviews, and discussion forums.
lay-lamidou is a town in Pyrénées-Atlantiques, which is in southwestern France.
Rebourg is a village in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of France.

A structure is an organized arrangement of elements. In the physical world, structures can be man-made objects like buildings and machines or natural ones such as plants, rocks, and chemicals. In the digital realm, they include data structures used in computer science and musical forms. Structures come in different types. One type is a hierarchy where parts are connected from top to bottom. Another is a network where many connections link together. Lastly, there's a lattice structure where elements connect based on their position next to each other.

Visibility in meteorology measures how far we can see an object or light clearly. It's reported in surface weather observations, often using meters or miles depending on the country. Visibility impacts all types of travel: roads, boats, and planes. Meteorological visibility talks about how clear the air is. At night, visibility is still the same as during the day for the same air quality.

The Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Belgium have several art museums in Brussels. These museums hold more than 20,000 artworks, including drawings, sculptures, and paintings that go back to the 1400s and continue up to now.

On November 14, 2017, soldiers from the Zimbabwe Defence Forces (ZDF) surrounded Harare and took control of key areas. They also took over the Zimbabwe Broadcasting Corporation. The next day, ZDF said it was not a coup and President Robert Mugabe was safe but needed to deal with "criminals" around him who were causing problems. Tensions in Mugabe's ruling party, ZANU-PF, led to this event. Former first vice-president Emmerson Mnangagwa, supported by the ZDF, was fighting against first lady Grace Mugabe and her G40 faction over who would become the next leader after Mugabe turned 93. Before troops entered Harare, ZDF chief Constantino Chiwenga said purging senior officials like Mnangagwa had to stop. On November 19, ZANU-PF removed Mugabe as party leader and made Mnangagwa the new leader instead. They set a deadline for Mugabe to resign by November 20 or face removal from office. Mugabe did not resign, so on November 21, parliament held an impeachment session. Later that day, Mugabe sent a letter saying he was stepping down as president. Phelekezela Mphoko became acting president. Mnangagwa became the new president on November 24, 2017.

Pat Hoyt Taylor Jr. (April 1, 1924 – April 22, 2018) was an American politician and lawyer. He worked as the speaker of the North Carolina House of Representatives and was the 26th lieutenant governor of North Carolina.
Dhillon is a group within the Jat people found among Sikhs in Punjab, India. Some famous people named Dhillon might belong to this group, but they don't have to.

Cosmology is the study of the universe, from its beginning with the Big Bang and its development over time. It looks at how the universe started, how it has changed, and what might happen in the future. The Big Bang theory explains these things based on science. The term "cosmology" was first used in English in 1656 by Thomas Blount and later by Christian Wolff in 1731. It can include beliefs from religion or myths about how the universe began and what might happen at the end of time, but is mainly studied by scientists like astronomers and physicists. Philosophers, especially those who study space and time and metaphysics, also look into cosmology because it shares some areas with philosophy. However, theories in physical cosmology can include both scientific ideas that are testable and non-scientific ones that may not be. Cosmology focuses on the entire universe, unlike astronomy which looks at individual stars and planets. Modern cosmology is mostly based on the Big Bang theory combined with particle physics to explain how the universe works. The most common model today is called the Lambda-CDM model. Some scientists say cosmology is like a "historical science" because when we look at distant parts of space, we are seeing those places as they were in the past due to the time it takes for light to travel.
L'île-Saint-Denys is a town near Paris. It is north of Paris and close to the city center. The town sits on an island in the Seine River, which is why it has this name.
Saint-Gervais-en-Belin is a village in Sarthe, which is in the Pays-de-la-Loire region. It is located in western France.

The Ontario New Democratic Party (NDP) is a social-democratic political party in Ontario, Canada. Since March 2009, Andrea Horwath has led this party, which currently forms the official opposition after the 2018 election. It is part of the federal New Democratic Party. Formed in October 1961 from the Cooperative Commonwealth Federation (Ontario section) and the Ontario Federation of Labour (OFL), the NDP was most successful outside Canada's western heartland for many years. Donald C. MacDonald led it to its first big win in 1967, when they elected 20 members to the Ontario Legislative Assembly. In 1975, under Stephen Lewis' leadership, the party became official opposition for the first time since the Cooperative Commonwealth Federation did so twice in the 1940s. After poor performance in the 1977 election, which led to losing second place, Lewis resigned and Michael Cassidy took over as leader. However, he only led one campaign before resigning after a poor 1981 election result. Bob Rae became the new leader in 1982. In 1985, his party held power with the Liberals by signing an agreement. After the 1987 general election, they again formed official opposition. The 1990 election surprisingly resulted in the NDP winning its first government in Ontario's history, making it Canada's first New Democratic Party provincial government east of Manitoba. However, economic issues led to their defeat in 1995 and Rae stepped down. Howard Hampton was elected leader at a 1996 convention and led for three elections. He lost official party status after the 1999 and 2003 elections but regained it after winning several by-elections in the mid-2000s. The NDP kept its status after the 2007 election, and Hampton stepped down in 2009. Andrea Horwath replaced him as leader after winning at a Hamilton convention in 2009. Under her leadership, they won 17 seats in 2011 and 21 seats in 2014. In the 2018 election, under Horwath's guidance, they gained 40 seats to form official opposition again.

Hans von Borsody was a German film actor. He was born on September 20, 1929, in Vienna, from a Hungarian descent family with artistic roots. His father, Edvard, was a film director, and his uncle Julius worked as a set designer. His daughter Suzanne became an actress. Borsody moved to Berlin when he was three years old and got German citizenship. He was married four times: to Karin Dittmann, Rosemarie Fendel, Alwy Becker, and Heide Keller.

In the Bengal region, a popular folk tale called "Saat Bhai Champa" or "Sat Bhai Chompa" exists. It first appeared in a book named Thakurmar Jhuli in 1907, published by Dakshinaranjan Mitra Majumder. The introduction to the book was written by Rabindranath Tagore, who won the Nobel Prize. In 1944, Bishnu Dey shared a more detailed version of the story under the name "Sat Bhai Champa." Several Bengali movies were made based on this tale. One movie, "Sat Bhai Chompa" from 1968, is considered one of the top ten Bangladeshi films by the British Film Institute.
Gidos Kokars was born on August 16, 1921, and died on March 10, 2017. He was a Latvian conductor. His twin brother, Imants Kokars, was also a conductor.

Sobek, also called Sebek, was an ancient Egyptian god with many roles. He was linked to crocodiles, especially those in the Nile and West Africa. Sobek could be shown as a crocodile or as a human with a crocodile head. He was connected to kingship, making things grow, and warriors. But he also protected people from dangers in the Nile. People often called on him for safety.

Very High Frequency (VHF) Omnidirectional Range (VOR) helps airplanes find their position and stay on course. Airplanes get information from fixed ground radio beacons using a receiver unit. VOR works with frequencies between 108.00 to 117.95 MHz in the VHF band. Developed starting in 1937, VOR became the standard air navigation system by 1946 and is used worldwide for both commercial and general aviation. By 2000, about 3,000 VOR stations were operating globally, with around 1,033 in the US; this number decreased to 967 by 2013 as GPS became more popular. A VOR ground station sends signals that rotate 30 times per second and a steady signal at 30 Hz. This helps airplanes find their direction from the beacon relative to magnetic north. Using signals from two different VOR stations, pilots can pinpoint their position. VOR coverage is limited to about 200 miles as it depends on line of sight between transmitter and receiver. Each station sends a VHF signal that includes navigation information, the station’s identifier in Morse code, and sometimes voice messages like station name, flight advisories, or live broadcasts.

A cave is a big space underground, large enough for a person to enter. Caves are often formed by weathering of rock and can go deep underground. The word "cave" can also refer to smaller openings like sea caves, rock shelters, or grottos. However, strictly speaking, a cave must be deeper than it is wide, while a rock shelter has a wider opening. Speleology is the study of caves and their environments. Visiting or exploring caves for fun can be called caving, potholing, or spelunking.

Giovanni Boccaccio was born on June 16, 1313, and died on December 21, 1375. He was an Italian writer and poet. Petrarch knew him as a friend. Boccaccio wrote many famous works, such as "The Decameron" and "On Famous Women." He mostly wrote imaginative literature in the Tuscan language. Some of his other works were written in Latin. His writing was special because he used realistic dialogue, unlike medieval writers who followed set patterns for characters and stories.

A Roman legion, called "legio" in Latin (meaning "military group" or "recruited soldiers"), was a big military unit. It had about 4,200 foot soldiers and 300 horsemen during the Republican era. Later, under the Empire, it grew to around 5,200 foot soldiers and 120 auxilia (supporting troops).

Meadowbank Stadium, officially named Meadowbank Sports Centre, was a sports facility in Edinburgh, Scotland. It replaced earlier venues like New Meadowbank and Old Meadowbank. The stadium was built for the 1970 Commonwealth Games and hosted them again in 1986, becoming the first to do so twice. The stadium also hosted football games regularly. From 1974 to 1995, it was home to a Scottish league team called Meadowbank Thistle. Edinburgh City played there from 1996 until 2016 when they joined the Scottish Professional Football League. Since 2013, Leith Athletic also used the nearby Meadowbank 3G artificial pitch. In early 2019, the stadium was demolished to make way for a new one. It was also used by Edinburgh Rugby from 2002 to 2004.

Fernando Sebastián Aguilar CMF, born on December 14, 1929, and who passed away on January 24, 2019, was a Spanish cardinal in the Roman Catholic Church. He was also the former archbishop of Pamplona y Tudela. Pope Francis made him a cardinal on February 22, 2014.
Farschweiler is a town in the Trier-Saarburg district, located in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany.
Inō Tadataka, born on February 11, 1745, and died on May 17, 1818, was a Japanese person who made maps. He is famous for creating the first map of Japan using new and improved surveying methods.

Clarke County is located in northeastern Georgia. According to the 2010 census, it had 116,714 people. Athens is its county seat and is a consolidated city-county with Clarke County. The Athens-Clarke County area is part of a larger metropolitan region that includes Atlanta and Sandy Springs.
Sant'Antonio means Saint Anthony in Italian. It usually refers to places named after Saint Anthony of Padua or Saint Anthony Abate.

Ross Batty was born on September 20, 1986, in England. He played rugby for Barnard Castle School and is now a professional rugby player. His main position is hooker. Ross currently plays for Bath in the Aviva Premiership. He joined Bath from Rotherham in 2010 and became a regular in their scrum. On February 2, 2018, he celebrated his 150th appearance for Bath, including cup matches. Ross renewed his contract with Bath on April 25, 2019. The length of the new contract was not disclosed. He played nine seasons for Bath before the end of the 2018-2019 season.

Observation involves actively getting information from something you are looking at. In living things, this means using senses like sight and touch. In science, it also includes using tools to see or record data. Observation can mean noticing if something is there or not, or measuring it with numbers.
