In 1965, "How to Murder Your Wife" was an American black comedy film from United Artists. George Axelrod produced it, Richard Quine directed it, and Jack Lemmon, Virna Lisi, and Terry-Thomas starred in it. Quine also directed Jack Lemmon in other films like "My Sister Eileen," "It Happened to Jane," "Operation Mad Ball," "The Notorious Landlady," and "Bell, Book and Candle." Mel Keefer drew the comic strip art featured in the film. He created newspaper comics such as "Perry Mason," "Mac Divot," and "Rick O'Shay." Alex Toth made a teaser comic strip in Keefer's style for ten days before the movie opened, running in "The Hollywood Reporter" and several newspapers.
Hiroshi Umemura, born on February 22, 1972, is from Japan. He is a fighter in mixed martial arts. He fought in both the bantamweight and featherweight categories.

Action Comics is an American comic book/magazine series that introduced Superman, a famous superhero. The company that published it was called National Allied Publications first, then changed to National Comics Publications and National Periodical Publications before becoming DC Comics. The original version of the comics ran from 1938 to 2011 and had issues numbered in sequence, making it one of the longest-running comic books. A second volume of Action Comics started with issue #1 in 2011 and ended in 2016. After that, the series returned to its original numbering starting from issue #957 in August 2016.
The Centre Étienne Desmarteau is a versatile building in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. It has two ice rinks.

Stephen Lewis, born on December 17, 1926, and passed away on August 12, 2015, was known as Stephen Cato early in his career. He worked as an actor, comedian, director, screenwriter, and playwright. People remember him most for playing Inspector Cyril "Blakey" Blake on a show called "The Buses." He also played Clem "Smiler" Hemmingway in "Last of the Summer Wine" and Harry Lambert in "Oh, Doctor Beeching!" Besides these roles, he acted in many stage and film productions.

In chemistry, a leaving group is a part of a molecule that goes away with an electron pair when a bond breaks. It can be an ion (like chloride, bromide, iodide, or sulfonate esters) or a neutral molecule (like water or ammonia). For the breaking to happen, it needs to stabilize extra electrons. Common ions that leave are halides such as chlorine, bromine, and iodine, and sulfonate esters like tosylate. Fluoride can also leave in some nerve agents. Neutral molecules that often leave include water and ammonia. Sometimes, positively charged parts of a molecule (like hydrogen released during benzene nitration) can act as leaving groups too. These are called electrofuges.

Caliban is the second-biggest irregular satellite that moves backward around Uranus. It was found on September 6, 1997, by Brett J. Gladman, Philip D. Nicholson, Joseph A. Burns, and John J. Kavelaars using a big telescope called the 200-inch Hale Telescope. At first, it had a temporary name, s/1997 U 1. Later, it was named Uranus XVI. This moon is called Caliban because it comes from a character in Shakespeare's play "The Tempest."

The German flag consists of three equal horizontal bands of black, red, and gold. It was first used as Germany's national flag in 1919 during the Weimar Republic until 1933. Since the mid-1800s, Germany has had two main sets of national colors: black-red-gold and black-white-red. Black-red-gold are the colors from the 1848 revolutions, the Weimar Republic (1919–1933), and the current federal republic (since 1949). The German Democratic Republic used these colors from 1949 to 1990 but added a socialist coat of arms in 1959. Black-white-red first appeared in 1867, during the North German Confederation, which included Prussia and other northern states. This state became known as the German Empire after including southern states from 1870–1871. It used these colors until 1918-1919. After that, black-white-red symbolized the political right. Nazi Germany revived these colors in 1933 along with their own swastika flag. After World War II, black-white-red was still used by some conservative groups or far-right groups because it is not forbidden like proper Nazi symbols. Black-red-gold is officially the flag of the Federal Republic of Germany. It is protected as an official symbol of the constitutional order, and according to German law, defaming it can result in a fine or up to five years in prison.

betrayal is the breaking or violation of a presumptive contract , trust , or confidence that produces moral and psychological conflict within a relationship amongst individuals , between organizations or between individuals and organizations . often betrayal is the act of supporting a rival group , or it is a complete break from previously decided upon or presumed norms by one party from the others . someone who betrays others is commonly called a traitor or betrayer . betrayal is also a commonly used literary element , also used in other fiction like films and tv series , and is often associated with or used as a plot twist .
Ile-d'Ale is a small town in Vendée, which is in Pays de la Loire. This region is located in western France.

Anna Kavan, born Helen Emily Woods on April 10, 1901, and passed away on December 5, 1968, was from Britain. She wrote novels and short stories and painted too. At first, she used the name Helen Ferguson for her publications. In 1939, she began using Anna Kavan as both a pen name and her legal name.

Hamont-Achel is a town in Belgium's Limburg province. It was formed in 1977 by combining the city Hamont and village Achel. On January 1, 2006, it had 13,770 people living there. The town covers 43. 66 square kilometers, making the population density about 315 people per square kilometer. It has an important Trappist abbey called Achel Abbey. Part of this abbey is a brewery named De Achelse Kluis, one of eleven Trappist breweries in the world. Professional tennis player Elise Mertens lives in Hamont-Achel.

In October 2015, an election took place to choose a new Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. This happened on October 29, during the 114th Congress. John Boehner, who was the previous Speaker, planned to resign on October 30. Boehner had been the first to step down in the middle of his term since 1989. This was the 124th election for a House Speaker since 1789. Paul Ryan, a Republican and chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, won with 236 votes. Nancy Pelosi, a Democrat and minority leader, got 184 votes, and others received 12 votes. To win, a candidate needed 217 votes. Paul Ryan was younger than any previous Speaker since James G. Blaine in 1869. After winning, Ryan gave his first speech as speaker-elect and was sworn in by John Conyers on October 30. Boehner had been Speaker since January 5, 2011. During his time, he faced many disputes with the Freedom Caucus. Before the election, Kevin McCarthy, who was House Majority Leader, seemed likely to win but withdrew when the Freedom Caucus refused to support him. The conference then voted for Paul Ryan after getting support from different party groups. On October 28, Ryan won the conference vote and became Speaker on October 29.
Hans-Peter Müller, known as Hansi, was born on July 27, 1957, in Stuttgart. He used to be a German football player and played as a midfielder.
St. Francis is a city in Clay County, Arkansas, United States. It is located near the St. Francis River. The city had 250 people living there according to the 2010 count.

jules henri poincaré (29 april 1854 – 17 july 1912) was a french mathematician, physicist, engineer, and philosopher. People say he was very talented in many fields of science and math. In mathematics, he was one of the last who could be an expert in all areas. poincaré made important contributions to math and physics. He worked on problems like the three-body problem and found a system that showed randomness in nature, which helped develop chaos theory. He is also seen as a founder of topology, a branch of math. in his work, poincaré noted how physical laws stay the same under different changes. He presented transformations called lorentz transformations in their modern form. Poincaré found more velocity transformations and wrote about them to lorentz in 1905. His work helped create special relativity theory. he also suggested gravitational waves exist, sending out from a body at light speed, needed for lorentz's theory. The poincaré group, used in physics and math, is named after him. early in the 20th century, he proposed what became known as the poincaré conjecture, an important unsolved problem in math until it was solved in 2002-2003 by grigori perelman.

Wellin is a Walloon municipality in Belgium, located in the province of Luxembourg. As of January 1, 2007, it had an area of 67.52 km² and 2,958 people living there. That means there were about 44 people per square kilometer. Wellin includes several smaller areas: Wellin itself, Chanly, Halma, Lomprez, and Sohier. Other towns nearby are Barzin, Froidlieu, Fays-Famenne, and Neupont.

Lynwood is a city in Los Angeles County, California. The population was 69,772 in the 2010 census, slightly down from 69,845 in 2000. Lynwood is close to South Gate and Compton in southern Los Angeles. It became an incorporated city in 1921. Lynwood is named after Lynn Wood Sessions, who was Charles Sessions' wife and a local dairy farmer. The nearby railroad station was also called Lynwood.
Trachselwald is a village in the Emmental region of the Swiss canton of Bern.

James Edward Westcott was an American photographer born on January 20, 1922, and died on March 29, 2019. He worked with the U.S. government in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, during the Manhattan Project and the Cold War. As one of few allowed to take photos there, he took many pictures of building and running the facilities at Oak Ridge and of everyday life for people living there.

Love and Basketball is a movie made in 2000. It is about romance and playing basketball. The film stars Sanaa Lathan and Omar Epps. In the story, Quincy McCalm, played by Epps, and Monica Wright, played by Lathan, are neighbors who both love basketball. They eventually fall in love. This movie was the first time Gina Prince-Bythewood directed a film. It came out on April 21, 2000, in the United States. People who watched it liked what they saw.

Like other games in the "Super Smash Bros." series, both "Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS" and "Super Smash Bros. for Wii U" are fighting games where players use different attacks to weaken their opponents and knock them out of an arena. These games include characters, items, music, and stages from various Nintendo franchises as well as some third-party ones. The development began in 2012 and was announced at E3 in 2013. The gameplay is balanced between the faster and more competitive "Super Smash Bros. Melee" and the slower and more casual-friendly "Super Smash Bros. Brawl." New features include up to eight players fighting together on the Wii U version, support for Nintendo's amiibo, using custom Miis as playable fighters, post-release downloadable content with new fighters and stages, and customizable special moves. Some features from previous games were removed, such as the story mode in "Brawl." Critics praised the fine-tuning of existing gameplay but had some issues with online play. Both versions sold well—over nine million copies for the 3DS version by December 2017, and over five million for the Wii U version during the same period. This game was followed by "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate" for Nintendo Switch in 2018.
guttert-Feschel is a town in the Leuk district, in the Valais canton, Switzerland. It became one town when Gutten and Feschel joined together in 2000.

Rafael Alkorta Martínez was born on September 16, 1968. He is a Spanish former footballer who mainly played as a central defender. Currently, he works as the sporting director for Athletic Bilbao. Alkorta played for Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid during his 17-year professional career. He made 370 La Liga appearances and scored eight goals. He helped Real Madrid win three trophies. He also played three times for the Spanish national team in World Cups during the 1990s.
Ryland Heights is a city in Kentucky. It's in Kenton County and is part of the Cincinnati area. The number of people living there increased from 799 in 2000 to 1,022 in 2010.
Dorothea Sally Eilers was an American actress. She lived from December 11, 1908, to January 5, 1978.
Matthias Lukas Ginter, born on January 19, 1994, is a German soccer player. He plays as a center back for Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Bundesliga and also represents the Germany national team.
A consumer buys items or services mainly for personal, social, family, or household use. They are not buying for a business.
wide awake means fully alert or conscious. It can also be written as wideawake.

Diving Machine G5 is a roller coaster at Janfusun Fancyworld, in Taiwan. It was made by Swiss company Bolliger & Mabillard in 2000. Diving Machine G5 was the second Dive Coaster built; the first one was called Oblivion and was at Alton Towers in the United Kingdom. This roller coaster is in the Sky Plaza section of the park. It looks almost like Oblivion, its predecessor. The name "Diving Machine G5" comes from the strong g-forces felt during the drop. Like Insane Speed, Diving Machine G5 has no theme. Along with Ku Ku and Insane Speed, it is one of three roller coasters at the park. Because it's close to the entrance, this ride gets long lines in the morning but shorter waits later in the day.

James W. Hardy III (December 24, 1985 – June 7, 2017) was a wide receiver in American football. He was chosen by the Buffalo Bills in the second round of the 2008 NFL draft. Hardy also played for the Baltimore Ravens. He went to Indiana University to play college football.
Koenigsegg Automotive AB makes very fast and exciting sports cars. They are located in Ängelholm, Skåne County, Sweden.

Alfredo Félix Aльcóн was an Argentine actor born in Buenos Aires on March 3, 1930. He worked as a film and theatre actor for over five decades. His first movie was "Love Never Dies" in 1955. He received many awards during his career, including the Silver Condor, the Martin Fierro Award, and the 1981 Diamond Konex Award. Alfredo Félix Aльcóн passed away on April 11, 2014, at the age of 84.

Uzbekistan joined the Olympics as an independent country in 1994. Since then, Uzbek athletes have competed in every Olympic Games. Before that, Uzbek athletes took part in the Olympics as part of the Soviet Union from 1952 to 1988. After the Soviet Union ended, Uzbekistan was on a unified team in 1992. Uzbek athletes have won 26 medals in summer Olympics mostly in wrestling and boxing. They also got one medal in winter Olympics. The country's Olympic committee was formed in 1992 and recognized by the IOC in 1993.

Brendan Halligan was born on July 5, 1936, and passed away on August 9, 2020. He was an Irish economist and politician. Halligan founded and led the Institute of International and European Affairs (IIEA), a think tank that focuses on European and international issues. In addition, he was president of the Ireland China Institute, an independent think tank in Dublin, Ireland, which started officially in October 2019. His career included work in both Irish public sector organizations and the private sector. At different times, Halligan held several important positions: he was the general secretary of the Labour Party, a Teachta Dála (TD) in Ireland's parliament, a senator, and a member of the European Parliament (MEP).

Ofterchwang is a town in southern Germany, specifically in Oberallgäu, Bavaria. It hosts professional winter sports events like World Cup alpine races. The area is known for skiing and other sports. Traditionally, the region was agricultural. Ofterchwang has a church with a World War II memorial, as well as small chapels. Nowadays, tourism is important in this area. In winter, people come to ski. During summer, hiking, mountain biking, and parachute flying are popular activities. Tourists also enjoy "dorfsabend," which features traditional Bavarian costumes, dancing, food, and beer.

The Cheongyang chili pepper, also called dang jo cheongyang, is a medium-sized variety of the capsicum annuum species. It has a heat level of 10,000 Scoville units. These peppers look like regular Korean chili peppers but are much spicier. Cheongyang chili peppers come from Cheongyang County in South Korea. However, they were developed by Dr. Yoo Il-Woong. He used local Jeju Island chilli and Thai chilli to create them. When young, the peppers can be light purple or green. As they ripen, they turn a deep red color. Even when dried, these peppers stay dark red.
grimbosq is a town in Calvados. Calvados is in Normandy, which is in western France.

Saliva, also called spit, is a fluid produced by the salivary glands in your mouth. In humans, it's mostly water but also contains electrolytes, mucus, white blood cells, and enzymes like amylase and lipase that help break down food. Saliva includes antimicrobial agents such as secretory IgA and lysozymes. These enzymes start breaking down the starches and fats from your food during digestion. They also clean food particles stuck between teeth, protecting them from bacteria. Saliva helps by making food wet so you can swallow it easily and keeps your mouth moist. Different animals use their saliva in unique ways. Some swifts build nests using sticky saliva. Certain snakes use venomous saliva to hunt, injecting it through fangs. Some caterpillars make silk from modified salivary glands.

Larkana district is in the Sindh province of Pakistan. The main city is Larkana. Two former Pakistani prime ministers, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto, come from this district. Another former leader, Mumtaz Ali Bhutto, was also born here. Actress Sohai Ali Abro and folk singer Abida Parveen are also from Larkana. The Larkana Bulls cricket team was started in 2013. Other towns in the area include Ratodero, Dokri, Bakrani, and Naodero. In 2005, under Prime Minister Pervez Musharraf, the district was split to form a new district called Qamber and Shahdadkot. This new district includes the towns of Qamber Khan and Shahdadkot.

The Eurocopter EC120 Colibri, now called Airbus Helicopters, is a small helicopter that can carry five people. It has one engine and is used for light duties. This helicopter was designed by Eurocopter, CATIC, HAIG, and STAERO in France. In China, the aircraft is made by Hamc as the HC120. They started making it locally in 2004 at their factory in Harbin, a city in northern China. Both the Chinese military and local police have bought these helicopters for use in China.

Madeleine Vionnet, born on June 22, 1876, in Loiret, France, died on March 2, 1975. She was a French fashion designer. Vionnet trained in London before returning to Paris in 1912 to open her first fashion house. It had to close during World War I but reopened after the war. Between 1919 and 1939, she became one of Paris's top designers. In 1939, her house closed again due to World War II, and Vionnet retired in 1940. Known as the "queen of the bias cut" and "the architect among dressmakers," Vionnet is famous for her elegant Grecian-style dresses and for popularizing the bias cut in fashion. Her work inspired many modern designers.
Kuthwal is one of the 51 union councils in Abbottabad district. This district is in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. It is situated northwest of Abbottabad city, which is the district capital.

Sir Joshua Reynolds was born on July 17, 1723, and died on February 23, 1792. He was an English painter who mainly painted portraits. John Russell said he was one of the most important painters in Europe during the 18th century. Reynolds believed in making paintings that looked perfect even though they weren't real life. In 1769, King George III made him a knight. Reynolds also helped found and became the first president of the Royal Academy of Arts.

This list shows current cities, towns, and unincorporated communities in New York state. It also gives the county names where each place is located. If there are zip codes, it includes the lowest and highest ones.

Gillingham Football Club is a professional soccer team from Gillingham, Kent, England. The "Gills" play at Priestfield Stadium. They are the only Kent-based team in the Football League and compete in League One, which is the third level of English football. Founded in 1893, they joined the league in 1920. In 1937–38, they were replaced by Ipswich Town but came back to the league 12 years later when it expanded from 88 to 92 teams. Twice in the late 1980s, they nearly won promotion to the second tier but then declined and narrowly avoided relegation to the Football Conference in 1993. From 2000 to 2005, Gillingham were in the second tier for the first time in their history, finishing eleventh in 2002–03.

Daniel Hudson Burnham was an American architect and urban designer, born on September 4, 1846, and died on June 1, 1912. He supported the "Beaux-Arts" movement. Some say he might have been the most successful leader in American architecture. Burnham was a well-known architect in Chicago. In 1892-93, he worked as director of works for the World's Columbian Exposition, often called "The White City." He played important roles in planning cities like Chicago, Manila, Baguio, and Washington D.C.'s downtown area. He also designed famous buildings such as skyscrapers in Chicago, New York City’s Flatiron Building, Union Station in Washington D.C., London's Selfridges department store, and San Francisco’s Merchants Exchange. While he is best known for his skyscrapers and city planning, about a third of Burnham's total work—14.7 million square feet (1.37 million square meters)—was dedicated to shopping buildings.
Vezot is a commune in Sarthe, which is in the Pays de la Loire region. It is located in western France.
Bizen's original center was in the city of Okayama now. From a very early time, Bizen became important for making swords in Japan.

Yandobinskoye is a small village in Russia's Chuvash Republic. It's part of Alikovsky District and located in the central area. The main administrative center nearby is called Yandoba. The population of Yandobinskoye was about 1,081 people as of 2006. This settlement includes twelve smaller rural areas. There is a road that goes through this village.

Jabalpur, known as Jubbulpore until 2006, is a major city in Madhya Pradesh, India. It's called Jabalpur officially now. In 2011, it was the third-largest urban area in Madhya Pradesh and the country’s 38th largest. Famous for Dhuandhar Falls and White Marble Rocks at Bhedaghat, some think snooker began here. Jabalpur is a big administrative, industrial, and business center in Madhya Pradesh. It's an important education place too. The state's high court and many government offices are there. With four main factories making weapons, it’s the city’s top job provider. Other smaller businesses exist. A major trade hub for forest products, Jabalpur grows quickly. As the biggest district in Madhya Pradesh, it has a division named after it. Historically, part of Kalachuri and Rajgond rule, it mixed cultures due to Mughals and Marathas later. In 1800s, British renamed it Jubbulpore. Since India's independence, there are calls for a new state called Mahakoshal with Jabalpur as its capital. The city hosts railway offices, power board, forestry research institute, and army headquarters for five states including Madhya Pradesh. Jabalpur is also home to the Grenadiers and Jammu and Kashmir Rifles army units, along with Signal Training Centre HQ.

In chemistry, an ester is a compound from an acid—organic or inorganic—where at least one hydroxyl group (-OH) is replaced by an alkoxy group. Esters are often made when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol. Fatty acid esters of glycerol, called glycerides, are crucial in biology as major lipids. They form most animal fats and vegetable oils. Esters with small molecular weight are frequently used as fragrances found in essential oils and pheromones. Phosphoesters build DNA molecules. Nitrate esters, like nitroglycerin, are known for their explosive nature. Polyesters, important plastics, consist of monomers bonded by ester groups. Esters typically have a sweet smell and work well as solvents for many plastics, plasticizers, resins, and lacquers. They are also widely used in synthetic lubricants.
People's Palace can mean:

Irrigation involves providing water to plants at the right times. It helps grow crops, keep landscapes looking good, and plant new areas when there's not much rain. Irrigation can also protect against frost, stop weeds from growing, and prevent soil from becoming too dense. In contrast, farming that depends only on rain is called rain-fed. Irrigation systems are used for more than just watering plants; they help cool animals, reduce dust, get rid of sewage, and assist in mining. Irrigation is often studied with drainage, which removes extra water from land. People have been using irrigation for over 5,000 years in different cultures around the world, including Asia and parts of America.

Parma is a city in northern Italy, in the Emilia-Romagna region. It's famous for its buildings, music, art, ham called prosciutto, cheese, and beautiful countryside. Parma has an old university, one of the oldest in the world. The city is split by a stream. The area on one side of the river is known as "oltretorrente". In ancient times, when the city was called Parma by the Etruscans, Romans used this name for their round shield. An Italian poet named Attilio Bertolucci, who came from a small village near Parma, wrote: "As a capital, it needed a river. As a smaller capital, it got a stream that is often dry."

A bottle cap or top seals a bottle's opening. It is usually brightly colored and has the brand logo. Plastic caps go on plastic bottles, while glass ones have metal with plastic backing; the metal part is usually steel. Some plastic caps have a pour spout. Flip-top caps provide controlled dispensing of dry products. Different types of plastic are often used for caps compared to bottles.

Kimble County is in Texas, United States. It is on the Edwards Plateau. In 2010, there were 4,607 people living there. The county seat is Junction. Kimble County was formed in 1858 and officially set up in 1876. It is named after George C. Kimble who died at the Battle of the Alamo.

The Salt Fork of the Arkansas River is a small river that joins the Arkansas River. It flows through southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma in the United States. Through the Arkansas River, it becomes part of the Mississippi River's larger water system.

John Elliot, born on May 6, 1898, and died on September 18, 1988, was a British railway manager. His birth name was John Elliot Blumenfeld. He was the son of R.D. Blumenfeld, who worked as the editor for the "Daily Mail." Later, R.D. became managing editor at the "Daily Express." In March 1923, John changed his last name to Elliot—his mother's surname—following advice from Lord Beaverbrook.
Tagusdorf is a commune in Haut-Rhin, which is in Alsace, in northeastern France.
In seismology, the epicenter is the spot on the ground directly above where an earthquake starts. This starting point is called the hypocenter or focus.

Elephant polo is played while riding elephants. It is popular in Nepal, Rajasthan (India), and Thailand. England and Scotland also have teams. Players use a standard ball and sticks made of bamboo. The field is smaller because the elephants move slower. Two people ride each elephant. One person directs the mahout, who steers the elephant. The player tells the mahout where to go and hits the ball. Elephant polo started in Meghauli, Nepal. Tiger Tops in Nepal organizes the game and hosts world championships. In Nepal and Thailand, rules are set by the World Elephant Polo Association (WEPA) to protect elephants. In India and Sri Lanka, events are run separately. An annual tournament was held in Galle, Sri Lanka, under a local association. In 2007, an elephant attacked during a game, hurting players and damaging equipment. Critics said the treatment of polo elephants was cruel. This led to games being canceled and sponsorship ending. Elephant polo records were removed from Guinness World Records. Thailand will stop hosting polo matches in October 2018. An annual tournament at Anantara Hotel Bangkok used to happen there, owned by Minor Hotels.

Eldorado is a city in Saline County, Illinois, United States. Its population was 4,122 at the 2010 census, peaking at 5,198 in 1980. The name "Eldorado" doesn't mean what it sounds like—it originally had a different spelling and meaning. It comes from the last names of two founders: Judge Samuel Elder and his son William, grandson Francis Marion, and neighbor Joseph Reed. Some sources say it was also spelled "elder-redo." According to legend, a signpainter for the railroad changed the name to "Eldorado" on the train depot in 1980. This new spelling has been used ever since, pronounced as "el-do-ray-doh." Eldorado is part of the Illinois-Indiana-Kentucky area and is a suburb within the Harrisburg micropolitan statistical area.
Ayn can mean:

Bihar Muslims are people from the Indian state of Bihar who follow Islam. Most Bihar Muslims belong to the Sunni branch of Islam. Even before the Mughal era, religious scholars and spiritual leaders in pre-Mughal Bihar were Sunnis. However, there is also a significant Shia Muslim community in Patna. This group descends from settlers who came from Lucknow in the 1800s.

Morehouse Parish is a place in Louisiana, USA. In 2010, it had about 27, 979 people. The main town is Bastrop. Morehouse Parish was created in 1844. It includes the Bastrop, LA micropolitan area, which is part of the Monroe–Ruston–Bastrop, LA combined statistical area.

Hurricane Gloria hit New England in 1985, the first big storm since Hurricane Agnes in 1972 and Hurricane Donna in 1960. It formed from a tropical wave in the Atlantic Ocean, became a hurricane on September 24, and reached very strong winds by September 27. Before hitting land, Gloria caused warnings for the East Coast from South Carolina to Maine. Many people left their homes as a safety measure. The strongest winds were mostly east of where the eye of the storm was, so northern areas like North Carolina and New Jersey were not as badly affected. But in Long Island and Connecticut, strong winds and falling trees knocked out power for over 4 million people. Some places on Long Island went without electricity for a long time, leading to major changes in local companies. Six people died because of fallen trees. In North Carolina, high waves destroyed many homes along the coast and caused beach erosion. Farther north, flooding closed some roads. Gloria also damaged crops worth about $20 million (1985 USD). Overall damage in the United States was estimated at $900 million, less than expected. In Canada, some areas had small power outages, but confusion over when the storm hit led to setting up a new hurricane center.

Colusa (formerly Colusi, Colusi's, Koru, and Salmon Bend) is the county seat of Colusa County, California. Its population was 5,971 in 2010, up from 5,402 in 2000. The name "Colusi" comes from the local Coru Native American tribe who lived on the other side of the Sacramento River in the 1840s.

The Shaolin temple, also known as Shaolin Monastery, is a Chan Buddhist temple in Dengfeng County, Henan Province, China. It's thought to have been founded in the fifth century and remains the main temple of the Shaolin school of Buddhism today. The temple is located west of Zhengzhou city. In 2010, it became part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site along with other historic monuments in Dengfeng.

The Singapore flag was adopted in 1959, the year Singapore became self-governing within the British Empire. It became the official flag again when Singapore separated from Malaysia on August 9, 1965. Before becoming independent, it was the only state flag in Malaysia with a different width to length ratio. The flag has two colors: red at the top and white below. In the top-left corner is a white crescent moon next to a five-pointed star. These symbols mean that Singapore is a young nation growing stronger, promotes equality among people, and stands for important national values. On water, ships do not use the national flag as their main flag. Instead, they fly a civil ensign with a red background having a white version of the crescent and stars symbol in the middle. Non-military government boats, like coast guard ships, fly a blue state ensign with the national flag in the top-left corner and an eight-pointed compass rose below it. Naval warships use a similar naval ensign but with a white background. There are rules about when and how to fly the Singapore flag. These rules now allow citizens to put the flag on their cars during holidays, and they can also display it at home anytime.

Aldgate is an Underground station in London, near Aldgate in the City of London. The station is on the Circle Line between two points and is at the end of the Metropolitan Line. It's in Travelcard Zone 1. Aldgate opened in 1876 with its entrance on Aldgate High Street. Later, a nearby station named opened eight years later. This new station is served today by the District and Hammersmith & City lines.
Strue is a town in Haut-Rhin, which is in Alsace, a region in northeastern France.
Dawson County is in Montana, U.S. The 2010 Census showed it had 8, 966 people. The main town is Glendive.

An illuminated manuscript has beautiful decorations like letters, borders, and small pictures. It’s often called a decorated or illustrated book from Western traditions. In the strictest sense, it refers to books with gold or silver decoration. But usually, people use this term for any beautifully decorated or illustrated book. The earliest known illuminated manuscripts date back to 400-600 AD in regions like the Ostrogoths and Eastern Roman Empire. These books were important because they helped keep written words alive when few could read. Monks in late antiquity saved much of ancient literature by copying it, shaping which texts survived. Illumination made old documents more valuable. In times when new rulers didn’t know to read the languages of these documents, this mattered a lot. Most existing manuscripts are from the Middle Ages or Renaissance. Many were religious books. From about 1200 AD, more non-religious texts also got decorated. Most medieval books were written on parchment made from animal skins like calf, sheep, or goat. The best quality parchment was called vellum and used for important documents. In late Medieval times, some books were written on paper. By the end of the Middle Ages, printing replaced most handwritten illuminated manuscripts. Some early printed books had spaces left for decorations, but printing spread quickly, making hand-illustration less common. Only wealthy people asked for illustrated books in the 1500s. Many illuminated manuscripts from the Middle Ages survive today. They are some of the best examples of medieval painting and well-preserved. For many periods and places, they are almost all we have of early artwork.
lion-sur-mer is a commune in Calvados. Calvados is in Normandy, which is in northwestern France.

Stopover is a place in Pike County, Kentucky, United States. It is near the intersection of Kentucky Route 194 and Kentucky Route 2062, east of a place called Phelps. Stopover used to have a post office with the zip code 41568. The name came from the first postmaster, who also owned a general store there. He would often invite people to "stop over" and visit him in his store. Today, Stopover has a small country store and four churches: Shepard Memorial Presbyterian Church, Stopover Church of God, Stopover Freewill Baptist Church, and Camp Creek Pentecostal Church.
Unionville is a city in Appanoose County, Iowa, United States. The 2010 census showed that it had 102 people living there.
San Francisco is a city-county located in California, United States. San Francisco can also mean:

The common toad, or European toad, often just called a toad (scientific name "Bufo bufo"), is found throughout much of Europe, except Ireland, Iceland, and some Mediterranean islands. It's also present in parts of western North Asia and a small area in northwestern Africa. This toad is part of a group that includes similar animals with a common ancestor. During the day, it stays hidden but becomes active at night when it hunts for insects. It moves slowly or jumps short distances on its stumpy legs and has bumpy, grayish skin. Although they are usually alone, in breeding season, many toads gather near specific ponds. Males compete with each other to mate with females. Eggs are laid in jelly-like strings in the water, then hatch into tadpoles. Over several months, these tadpoles grow and develop, eventually sprouting legs and transforming into small toads. After leaving the water, young toads live mostly on land for their lives. The common toad is declining in some areas but is still listed as "least concern" by the IUCN Red List. It faces threats like habitat loss, especially drainage of breeding sites, and road deaths during its annual migrations. Toads have long been linked with witchcraft in popular culture.

HTC Corporation is a computer company based in Xindian, New Taipei City, Taiwan. It was founded in 1997. HTC makes and designs laptops and smartphones. Initially, it used Windows Mobile for its smartphones but later became part of the Open Handset Alliance to develop Android. Their first phone with Android was called the HTC Dream or T-Mobile G1. Despite initial success, competition from other companies like Apple and Samsung reduced HTC's market share to 7.2% by April 2015. The company has been making losses since then. In 2016, HTC started working on virtual reality technology and created the HTC Vive platform with Valve. After working with Google on its Pixel smartphone, HTC sold most of its design team and some smartphone-related ideas to Google for a billion dollars in 2017.

Samún (in Pontic Greek, it's called Sampsúnta) is a city on Turkey's northern Black Sea coast. About 1.4 million people live there. It’s the capital of the Samsun province and an important port. The growing city has two universities, several hospitals, shopping malls, many small factories, sports centers, and even an opera house. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk started the Turkish War of Independence from here in 1919.
Garden Valley is a town in Jackson County, Wisconsin, United States. The 2000 census showed 406 people lived there. North Branch is an unincorporated community within Garden Valley.

The national football team of Ireland plays men's international soccer. It is controlled by the Football Association of Ireland (FAI). The team first appeared at the 1924 Summer Olympics, reaching the quarter-finals. They were known as the Irish Free State from 1924 to 1936 and then called Éire or Ireland until 1950. In 1953, FIFA decided that in official matches for tournaments, both teams would be named the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. Northern Ireland could still use "Ireland" in some competitions until 1984. The Republic of Ireland first beat England at home in a match in Liverpool in 1949. They also reached the quarter-finals of the 1964 European Nations' Cup, losing to Spain. Under Jack Charlton's leadership, the team had its most successful period: they ranked sixth in FIFA rankings in August 1993 and qualified for UEFA Euro 1988 and the 1990 World Cup. They reached the quarter-finals of the 1994 World Cup as well. After Charlton, Mick McCarthy failed to qualify for the next three major tournaments but managed to get to the 2002 World Cup and UEFA Euro 2016 with Martin O'Neill. The team plays at home in Dublin's Aviva Stadium, though sometimes they play elsewhere in Ireland. The current coach is Stephen Kenny, and Séamus Coleman is their captain.
Special spelling means using a word in a different, not usual way on purpose to make it interesting.

Red Bank is a town in Monmouth County, New Jersey. It was incorporated in 1908 and is situated by the Navesink River. As of 2010, the population was 12,206, an increase from 11,844 in 2000 and 10,636 in 1990. Red Bank originally became a town on March 17, 1870, from parts of Shrewsbury Township. Then, on February 14, 1879, it was made into Shrewsbury City but regained its independence by May 15, 1879. Red Bank got its name because the soil along the Navesink River is red.

Michael Andrew Gove, born Graeme Andrew Logan on August 26, 1967, is a British politician. He became Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster in 2019 and Minister for the Cabinet Office in 2020. Gove has been representing Surrey Heath as an MP since 2005. A member of the Conservative Party, he held various positions such as Education Secretary from 2010 to 2014, Chief Whip from 2014 to 2015, Justice Secretary from 2015 to 2016, and Environment Secretary from 2017 to 2019. He tried twice to become leader of the Conservative Party in 2016 and 2019 but did not win. Gove studied at Robert Gordon's College and Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford. Before joining politics, he worked as an author and journalist for The Times. In 2005, he entered the House of Commons. He was part of the Shadow Cabinet under David Cameron from 2007 to 2010, serving as Shadow Secretary of State for Children, Schools and Families. As Education Secretary, Gove ended a previous government's building schools program, reformed A-levels and GCSEs by removing coursework, and dealt with the Trojan Horse scandal. During his term, he faced criticism from teaching unions. In 2014, he became Chief Whip. After the 2015 election, he moved to Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor roles. Gove played a key role in the Brexit referendum as co-convenor of Vote Leave with Boris Johnson. He later supported Boris Johnson's bid for Prime Minister but withdrew his support and ran for leadership himself. After Theresa May became Prime Minister, Gove left the cabinet. However, he returned to office as Environment Secretary after the 2017 election. In 2019, he attempted to become Conservative Party leader again but finished third. When Boris Johnson became Prime Minister in 2019, Gove was appointed Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster and took on additional responsibilities related to Brexit preparations.

Frode Johnsen was born on March 17, 1974. He is from Norway and used to play professional football. Frode played for teams like Odd and Rosenborg in Norway’s top league, the Tippeligaen. He also played for Nagoya Grampus and Shimizu S-Pulse in Japan. Frode was good at playing as a striker or midfielder. Standing 188 cm tall, he was strong at heading the ball. In his last season with Odds BK in 2015, Frode won an honor award for his long career. He retired when he was 41 years old. In 2013, Frode became the top scorer in Tippeligaen. This made him the oldest player to be the top scorer in a European league ever.

The town of Del Norte is in Colorado, United States. It is an important town because it has the county seat of Rio Grande County. The name is usually said like this: "DEL-nort." In 2010, there were 1,686 people living in the town.
angels in the outfield means: players catching fly balls in the outfield.

Karnali Zone was one of Nepal's fourteen zones, located in the mid-western region. Its headquarters were in Jumla. Karnali Zone was among Nepal's poorest and most remote areas, with limited road access. Most districts had airfields, except Kalikot, which was connected to Jumla Airport by seasonal roads. Karnali Zone was the largest zone in Nepal and included two national parks. Shey Phoksundo National Park, home to the deepest lake in Nepal (Phoksundo Lake), featured snow leopards and covered 3,555 square kilometers. Rara National Park surrounded Rara Lake, which was the biggest lake in Nepal at 10.2 square kilometers and known as "the Pearl of Nepal." Karnali Zone was divided into five districts. Starting in 2015, these districts were renamed as Karnali Pradesh.

Grandval is a municipality in the Jura Bernois area, which is part of the canton of Bern in Switzerland. It is in the French-speaking region called the Bernese Jura (Jura Bernois). Grandval was also known by its German name "Granfel" or "Granfelden," but people no longer use these names commonly.

Mario Altmann was born on November 4, 1986. He is from Austria and plays ice hockey professionally. Now, he plays for a team called EHC Black Wings Linz in the Austrian Hockey League (EBEL). Before that, he played for another team named EC VSV for five seasons. In April 2015, Altmann signed with EHC Black Wings Linz. Altmann is part of Austria's national ice hockey team. He played in the 2009 and 2011 IIHF World Championships and also participated in the 2014 Winter Olympics.

cee lo green released his first Christmas studio album on October 29, 2012, in the UK. It was called "Cee Lo's Magic Moment" and it was his fourth studio album overall. The album came out in the US one day later, on October 30, 2012, through Elektara Records. In December 2012, Cee Lo's versions of "Mary, Did You Know?" and "What Christmas Means to Me" reached number 22 and 23 on the R&B songs chart in the US. The album sold 181,000 copies in the United States in 2012. This was Cee Lo Green's first solo album without a parental advisory label.

Swatch Internet Time, also known as.beat time, is a way of measuring time introduced by the Swatch Corporation in 1998. It divides a day into 1000 parts called "beats." Each beat equals one minute and 26.4 seconds, or 86.4 seconds in standard time. Times are shown as three-digit numbers out of 1000 after midnight. For example, @248 means 248 beats after midnight, which is about 5 hours and 57 minutes. Swatch Internet Time doesn't have different time zones. Instead, it uses Biel Meantime (BMT), based on the headquarters of Swatch in Biel, Switzerland. BMT is the same as Central European Time, West Africa Time, and UTC+01. Unlike civil time in many countries, including parts of Europe, Swatch Internet Time does not change for daylight saving time.

The December 2010 North American blizzard affected parts of the United States and Canada from December 5 to December 29, 2010. In Europe, it was known as "Windstorm Benjamin" from January 4 to January 15. It was the first big winter storm of the 2010-11 season in North America and the fifth blizzard that year. The storm hit major cities like Norfolk, Philadelphia, Newark, New York City, Hartford, Providence, and Boston. It brought a lot of snow to these areas.
Sandslåne is a small place in Kramfors, which is in Västernorrland County, Sweden. It had 272 people living there in 2010.
Heinrich Ludwig Futterer, born on October 14, 1931, and passed away on February 10, 2019, was a German athlete. He mostly ran sprint races.

To Catch a Killer is a movie that aired in two parts in 1992. Eric Till directed it. Brian Dennehy and Michael Riley acted in it. The story is based on the true tale of catching American serial killer John Wayne Gacy.
Gianni Morandi, born on December 11, 1944, is an Italian singer, actor, and performer.

San Carlos is a community and census-designated place in Hidalgo County, Texas. Its population was 3,130 according to the 2010 United States Census. It's part of the McAllen-Edinburg-Mission metropolitan statistical area. San Carlos is located northeast of McAllen.

Crystal Palace Football Club is in Selhurst, South London, England. They play in the Premier League, which is the highest level of English football. The club was officially founded in 1905 but says it came from an amateur team started in 1861 by the same Crystal Palace company. This would make them one of the oldest professional clubs globally. Both the original and later clubs were linked to the Crystal Palace exhibition building. The professional team played there until 1915 when they moved because of World War I. In 1924, they got their current home at Selhurst Park. The amateur club was part of the Football Association since 1863 and took part in the first FA Cup in 1871–1872, reaching the semi-finals. After that, it disappeared from records. In 1905, Crystal Palace became a professional team. They tried to join the Football League but failed and joined the Southern League instead. In 1920, they finally joined the Football League. They mostly played in the top two divisions of English football since then. Since 1964, they only dropped below second place for three seasons between 1974 and 1977. Crystal Palace had a good period in the 1980s and early 1990s when they finished third in the league in 1990–91. In that same season, they almost qualified for the UEFA Cup but missed out due to limited European spots available to English clubs after the Heysel disaster. Crystal Palace joined the Premier League in 1992 and have been there since. They were runners-up twice in the FA Cup, losing to Manchester United both times in 1990 and 2016. The club's colors changed from claret and blue in 1973 to red and blue stripes they use now. Crystal Palace has a long rivalry with Brighton & Hove Albion for the M23 derby title, as well as rivalries with other south London clubs like Millwall and Charlton Athletic.

Richard Falk was born on November 13, 1930. He is an American professor who teaches international law at Princeton University. He has written or co-written 20 books and edited or co-edited another 20 volumes. In 2008, the United Nations Human Rights Council chose Richard Falk to be a special rapporteur for six years. His job was to look into human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967.

Consumer confidence measures how optimistic people feel about the economy and their money. If consumers feel good about the near future, they will spend more rather than save. When consumer confidence is high, people buy more things. When it's low, people save more and spend less. This optimism changes monthly based on how they think they can find jobs and see the current economic situation. Consumer confidence usually goes up when the economy grows and down when it shrinks. In the U.S., this measure often follows stock market performance with a delay.

Sheikh Ahmed Ismail Hassan Yassin (1937–2004) was a Palestinian imam and politician. He founded Hamas, an Islamic Palestinian military group and political party. Yassin also led the spiritual part of Hamas. Hamas became popular in Palestinian society by setting up charities that funded hospitals, education, libraries, and other services. However, it is also known for carrying out attacks against Israeli civilians. Many countries, including Europe, Israel, Japan, Canada, and the United States, considered Hamas a terrorist organization. Yassin was paralyzed from the chest down after a sports accident when he was 12 years old. He could hardly see. He used a wheelchair for his whole life. He died when an Israeli helicopter shot him during morning prayers. This attack killed both his guards and nine other people near him. His death received strong criticism worldwide. Over two hundred thousand Palestinians attended his funeral.
Ternouwen is a city and municipality in southwest Netherlands. It's located in Zeeland, specifically in Zeelandic Flanders. With more than 55,000 people, Ternouwen has the most residents in Zeeland.

The Queanbeyan River is a permanent stream in the Molonglo catchment, part of the Murray–Darling Basin. It's located in Monaro and Capital Country regions of New South Wales and Australian Capital Territory in Australia. The river is long and has a catchment area. It helps provide clean water for Canberra and Queanbeyan. This water is protected by federal laws. Some people think local Aborigines called it "Queanbeyan" because the word means "clearwater."

The king's gambit starts with White giving a pawn to move Black's e-pawn. If Black accepts, White has two main strategies. One is to play d4 and bxf4, regaining the pawn and controlling the center. Another is nf3 and bc4 followed by 0-0, creating an open f-file for White to attack Black’s weak f7 pawn. To keep the gambit pawn, Black might need to weaken their position with moves like g5 or unusual piece placements. A downside is that White's king becomes weaker too, facing a potential threat of qh4+. With Black having a pawn on f4, White can't usually respond to check with g3. If forced to move the king, it loses the right to castle safely. The king's gambit is an old opening, first studied by Italian chess player Giulio Cesare Polerio in the 17th century and featured in Luis Ramírez de Lucena’s book from 1497. This gambit was popular until the late 1800s due to better defensive play. Today, it's rarely seen at high levels but remains common among amateur players.

A hedgehog is any small, spiny mammal in the family Erinaceidae. There are 17 types of hedgehogs spread across five groups, found in parts of Europe, Asia, Africa, and New Zealand. They aren't native to Australia or North America, though some once lived there. Hedgehogs share a distant ancestry with shrews, with possible links to gymnures. These animals haven't changed much over 15 million years. Like early mammals, hedgehogs are mostly active at night for protection. Their spines look similar to those of porcupines and echidnas, but these creatures aren't related.

Mary Fallin (born December 9, 1954) is an American politician. She served as Oklahoma's 27th governor from 2011 to 2019. A Republican, she was first elected in 2010 and re-elected in 2014. Fallin began her political career by being elected to the Oklahoma House of Representatives in 1990. She served two terms there, from 1990 to 1995. In 1994, she became Oklahoma's 14th Lieutenant Governor and was re-elected twice more, serving under two governors until 2007. In 2006, Fallin ran for the U.S. House of Representatives from Oklahoma’s 5th district after Republican Ernest Istook announced he would retire. She won this election and served in Congress from 2007 to 2011. Fallin then ran for governor in 2010. In the primary, she got 54% of the votes against three other candidates. She beat the Democratic nominee, Lieutenant Governor Jari Askins, with 60% in the general election. She was re-elected in 2014, beating Oklahoma State Representative Joe Dorman. Fallin’s time as governor faced many problems and disagreements. In an October 2018 poll, she had a low approval rating of 17%, making her the least popular governor in the country. Because of term limits, she could not run for another term in 2018. Kevin Stitt became the new governor instead.

An echinoderm is a type of sea creature belonging to the phylum Echinodermata. The name comes from Greek, meaning "hedgehog skin." These animals are usually symmetrical with five parts and include starfish, urchins, sand dollars, cucumbers, and sea lilies. You can find echinoderms in oceans at all depths. There are about 7000 living species of echinoderms, making them the second-largest group after chordates (which include vertebrates like birds, fish, mammals, and reptiles). Echinoderms live both deep in the ocean and closer to the surface. They can reproduce by splitting themselves or regrow parts they lose. These animals are important because their hard skeletons make up much of the limestone found in rocks. They were often used for studying how animals grow back body parts. Some scientists believe that echinoderms played a big role in changing ocean life during the Mesozoic era.

Exology Chapter 1: The Lost Planet is Exo's first live album. It came out on December 22, 2014. SM Entertainment released it. There are two CDs with 36 songs in total (18 on each CD). Each member of the group has individual tracks, and some songs have remix versions in Korean and Mandarin or vice versa. The album had normal and special editions.

Bill Moggridge, who lived from June 25, 1943, to September 8, 2012, was a British designer. He helped start the design company IDEO and was also in charge of the Cooper-Hewitt National Design Museum in New York. Moggridge was one of the first people to focus on designing things for people. He created the term "interaction design" and made it widely used. Some of his work includes designing the first laptop, called the Grid Compass. He received awards like the National Design Award for lifetime achievement and the Prince Philip Designer Prize. Moggridge once said that his interest in how people interact with objects was central to his work.

The Blossoms are an American girl-group from California. In the 1960s, their most famous members were Darlene Love, Fanita James, and Jean King. The group made its own records but is best known for singing on hit songs. They recorded "He's a Rebel," which Phil Spector credited to The Crystals. The Blossoms provided backing vocals for many big hits from the 1960s. In terms of their importance, The Blossoms were like The Sweet Inspirations on the East Coast and The Andantes for Motown.

Earl Wilbur Sutherland Jr., born on November 19, 1915, in Burlingame, Kansas, was an American scientist who studied medicines and chemicals. He won a Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1971. His discovery was about how hormones work, especially epinephrine, using something called second messengers, specifically cyclic AMP.
Gevelsberg is a town in Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis. It is located in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Patrick James Riley, born March 20, 1945, is an American who worked as a basketball executive and coach in the NBA. He became the Miami Heat's president in 1995 and coached them twice (1995-2003, 2005-2008). As a player, Riley was part of the Lakers' championship team in 1972. Riley is known as one of the best NBA coaches ever. He led five championship teams: four with the Los Angeles Lakers during their "Showtime" era in the 1980s and one with the Heat in 2006. He was named Coach of the Year three times—once each for coaching the Lakers, New York Knicks, and Miami Heat. Riley also coached nine NBA All-Star games: eight times as head coach of the Western conference team (1982-1990) with the Lakers and once as head coach of the Eastern conference team in 1993 with the Knicks. He was the first North American sports figure to win a championship as a player, assistant coach, head coach, and executive. In 1996, Riley was one of the ten greatest coaches in NBA history. He helped the Heat win championships again in 2012 and 2013 while being their team president. In recognition of his achievements, he received the Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award from the NBA Coaches Association on June 20, 2012.

Meresankh I (she loves life) was an ancient Egyptian queen who married King Huni, the last ruler of the 3rd dynasty. She was also the mother of King Sneferu. Her name appears on a piece of the Palermo Stone and might be associated with an estate in Saqqara mentioned in the tomb of Pehernefer. Meresankh I is named alongside her son Sneferu in some writings found in the Pyramid Temple at Meidum. These writings date back to the time of King Tuthmosis III, who ruled during the 18th dynasty. The text includes a "hetep di nesu" text for both King Sneferu and Queen Meresankh.

Lipscomb County is in Texas, a state in the U.S. The 2010 census showed its population was 3,302 people. Lipscomb is the county seat. The county was formed in 1876 and organized in 1887. It was named after Judge Abner Smith Lipscomb, who was a secretary of state for the Republic of Texas.
In United States politics and government, the term "presidential nominee" has two different meanings.

The mighty Bosstones, or simply Bosstones, is an American ska punk band from Boston, Massachusetts. They started in 1983. Since then, lead singer Dicky Barrett, bassist Joe Gittleman, saxophonist Tim Burton, and dancer Ben Carr have been constant members. The lineup also includes Joe Sirois on drums, Leon Silva on saxophone, Lawrence Katz on guitar, John Goetchius on keyboards, and Chris Rhodes on trombone. The Bosstones are known as pioneers of ska punk and creators of its subgenre ska-core, which mixes ska with punk rock and hardcore. Starting from their 1989 album "Devil's Night Out," they toured and recorded a lot in the 1990s. They were influential in developing American third-wave ska music and became popular in mainstream music. Their biggest hit was "The Impression That I Get" from their 1997 album "Let's Face It." By December 2003, they had released seven studio albums, three EPs, and a live album before taking a break. In 2007, the Bosstones reunited and have since made three more studio albums. They've hosted an annual music festival called Hometown Throwdown in Boston since 1994, which runs around Christmas time.
Rickenbach is the name of some places. In Germany, there are none. In Switzerland, it exists.

In 2001, there was an American movie based on Beverly Donofrio's autobiography. The story is about a woman who faced challenges, including becoming a teenage mother, but later got her master's degree. The film covers events from 1961 to 1986 and stars Drew Barrymore, Steve Zahn, Brittany Murphy, and James Woods. This was the last movie directed by Penny Marshall. While Beverly Donofrio helped make the movie, some details in the film are different from her book.

The Limbourg brothers (Herman, Paul, and Johan) were famous Dutch miniaturists. They lived and worked from about 1385 to 1416 in Nijmegen. In the early 15th century, they painted in France and Burgundy. Their art style was called International Gothic. They are well-known for creating the "Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry," which is a famous late medieval illuminated manuscript.

Melissa Suzanne McBride was born on May 23, 1965. She is an American actress and used to be a casting director. Her biggest role came when she played Carol Peletier in the TV show "The Walking Dead" (from 2010 until now). People really liked her performance, and she won several awards and nominations. At first, McBride was only in a small part of the show, and her name appeared after the credits. But as time went on, her role grew bigger. By 2020, she was one of the main characters, appearing second in the opening credits. She also acted in every season of the show, along with Norman Reedus.
Willis David Gradison Jr., born on December 28, 1928, is a politician from Ohio. He worked in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 until 1993.

ronald sidney tauranac, born on January 13, 1925, and passed away on July 17, 2020, was an engineer and racing car designer from Britain and Australia. He co-founded the Brabham team with Formula One driver Jack Brabham in 1962. After Jack retired as a driver at the end of the 1970 season, Ronald owned and managed the Brabham team until 1972. In 1973, he helped redesign a racing car for Frank Williams. Later, he assisted Trojan in creating a Formula One version of their Formula 5000 car. After taking a short break in Australia, Tauranac returned to England. He started the Ralt marque in 1973, using a name his brother had used earlier. The first Ralt design was the RT1 chassis for Formula Three, Two, and Atlantic racing. This chassis proved successful, winning the European Formula Three championship in 1975 with Australian driver Larry Perkins. The RT1 chassis also won success in the 1978 season when Jan Lammers secured the European F3 title. In 1978, Tauranac designed the Theodore racing F1 car for the same year. For 1979, he created two new designs: the RT2 for Formula Two and the RT3 for Formula Three. The RT3 won five consecutive British F3 titles in 1983 with Pierluigi Martini at the wheel. A partnership with Honda led to the RH6 chassis, which won championships in 1981, 1984, and 1985. In October 1988, Tauranac sold Ralt to March Engineering for £1.25 million. After leaving Ralt, he continued working on various projects, such as racing school cars for Honda, designing a Formula Renault car, and consulting for the Arrows Formula One team. He also stayed involved with Honda. In 2002, Tauranac was honored by being appointed an Officer of the Order of Australia for his contributions to motor racing through engineering design, providing young drivers opportunities, and sharing knowledge with others for sport advancement. Ronald Tauranac died on July 17, 2020, at the age of 95.

The National Symphony Orchestra (NSO) was formed in 1930. It is a symphony orchestra from America, located in Washington, D.C. Their main performance place is the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The NSO played at the National Memorial Day concert and also performed at the Capitol Fourth.

On July 15, 2020, around 8:00 PM UTC, about 130 popular Twitter accounts were hacked. Hackers used these accounts to promote a bitcoin scam. Twitter and other news sources said the attackers got access to Twitter’s tools. They could change the tweets directly. The hackers might have tricked some employees into giving them access. Three people were arrested on July 31, 2020. They were charged with fraud, money laundering, identity theft, and unauthorized computer use related to the scam. In the scam, attackers asked people to send bitcoin to a wallet, promising they would get it back doubled as a gift. Within minutes of the first tweet, over 320 transactions had happened on one wallet address. Twitter removed the scam tweets before many more people sent money. Hackers also got data from eight non-verified accounts. Dmitri Alperovitch, who started CrowdStrike, called it “the worst hack of a major social media platform yet.” The FBI and other law enforcement are looking into this. They want to know how Twitter’s security works. Researchers worry that hackers might use similar tricks in important discussions online, like before the 2020 U.S. presidential election.

Madeline Gail Kahn, born Madeline Gail Wolfson on September 29, 1942, and passed away on December 3, 1999, was an American actress and comedian. She was known for her funny roles in movies like "What's Up, Doc?" (1972), "Young Frankenstein" (1974), "High Anxiety" (1977), "History of the World, Part I" (1981), as well as her award-nominated performances in "Paper Moon" (1973) and "Blazing Saddles" (1974). Kahn first appeared on Broadway in "Leonard Sillman's New Faces of 1968." She received Tony Award nominations for the plays "In the Boom Boom Room" (1974) and "On the Twentieth Century" (1978). In a short TV show called "Oh Madeline," she played Madeline Wayne from 1983 to 1984. For an ABC special, she won a Daytime Emmy Award in 1987. She was nominated for another Tony Award in 1989 and finally won the 1993 Tony Award for Best Actress for her role in "The Sisters Rosensweig." Other films she acted in include "The Cheap Detective" (1978), "City Heat" (1984), "Clue" (1985), and "Nixon" (1995).

Ji Guobiao, born on March 1, 1932, and died on September 5, 2019, was a Chinese chemical engineer. He became an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. Ji Guobiao was a pioneer in chemical fiber engineering technology in China.

The British Association for Applied Linguistics (BAAL) is a society where people interested in language and applied linguistics can meet. BAAL organizes regular meetings at different places in the UK, publishes conference proceedings, sends out a newsletter regularly, and gives scholarships to students. There is an elected group that represents members' interests. The current chair for 2018-2021 is Dawn Knight. BAAL has over 1200 members from around the world and is a registered charity in the UK (charity number 246800).

Halabja is a city in Kurdistan and the capital of Halabja governorate. It is located in Iraq, northeast of Baghdad and close to the Iranian border. The city sits at the base of what is often called the Greater Hewraman region, which spans across the Iran-Iraq border. To the northeast of Halabja are the Hawraman and Shnrwe ranges, in the south lies the Balambo range, and to the west flows the Sirwan River. Most people in Halabja speak Sorani Kurdish, but some villagers nearby use the Hewrami dialect.

The Russian Empire covered large parts of Eurasia and North America from 1721 until 1917, when a republic was declared. It was one of the largest empires ever, covering three continents—Europe, Asia, and North America. The empire was bigger than most others at that time, only smaller than the British and Mongol Empires. The Russian Empire grew strong while its neighbors weakened. For example, it defeated Napoleon's plans in 1812-1814 and expanded towards western and southern territories. From 1721 to 1762, the Romanov family ruled the empire, followed by the House of Holstein-Gottorp-Romanov from 1762 until the end. At its largest, in the early 19th century, the Russian Empire stretched from the Arctic Ocean to the Black Sea and westward into Alaska and northern California. It had about 125 million people when counted in 1897, making it one of the most populous countries then. The empire was very diverse, with many different economies, ethnic groups, languages, and religions. Over time, there were many uprisings and assassinations that the secret police watched closely. The economy mainly relied on farming, where peasants worked large estates as "serfs," tied to the land in a feudal system. They gained freedom in 1861, but nobles still controlled much of the land. The empire's territory was ruled by nobles called boyars until the rise of Emperor Ivan III (ruled 1462-1505), who greatly expanded it and laid its foundations. Peter the Great (ruled 1682-1725) continued this expansion, made St. Petersburg the capital, and brought Western ideas to Russia. Catherine the Great (ruled 1762-1796) also expanded and modernized the empire in a Western style. Alexander II (ruled 1855-1881) freed all serfs but kept aristocrats in power. He helped protect Orthodox Christians in Eastern Europe. By 1914, this led Russia to join World War I against Germany and its allies. The Russian Empire was run as an absolute monarchy based on the ideas of Orthodoxy, Autocracy, and Nationality until 1905 when it became a constitutional monarchy. It struggled during World War I, and in 1918, the Bolsheviks executed the royal family and took power after a civil war against the "White Army." They exiled or executed most nobles and ended up forming the Soviet Union in 1922.

Roberts County is a county in Texas, U.S. According to the 2010 census, it has 929 people, making it the least populous county in Texas after six others. Its main town is Miami, which is also the only city in the county. Roberts County was formed in 1876 and became an official county in 1889. It's named after Oran Milo Roberts, who was a governor of Texas. Notably, Roberts County is one of six counties in Texas that don't allow alcohol.

chopicallqui, possibly from "chawpi" meaning "center" and "kallki" meaning "ravine," is a mountain in Peru's Andes. It’s located in the Cordillera Blanca area and has an elevation of more than sea level. This makes it one of the highest peaks in Cordillera Blanca. The mountain is in Yungay province, in Ancash. It sits between Huascarán and Contrahierbas mountains.

Wofford Heights is a census-designated place in Kern County, California. It is part of the southern Sierra Nevada area. Wofford Heights is in the West Kern River Valley and is south-southwest of Kernville. The elevation is not specified. In 2010, it had 2,200 people, down from 2,276 in 2000.

Shakib Khan, born on March 28, 1979, is an actor, producer, singer, film organizer, and media personality from Bangladesh. He has been active in the film industry for about two decades, particularly in Dhallywood, which is a popular term for Bangladeshi films. Known as "King Khan" and "King of Dhallywood," he is one of the top-paid actors in Bangladesh. His career began with the 1999 film "Ananta Bhalobasha." However, it was the 2008 film "Priya Amar Priya," where he played a college student, that brought him widespread fame and success, earning him significant remuneration. "Shikari," released in 2016, received positive reviews from both audiences and critics. His roles in films like "Swatta" (2017) and "Nabab" further boosted his popularity, with "Nabab" becoming one of the highest-grossing Bangladeshi films ever. In 2019, he starred in the film "Nolok," for which he was paid a record amount. Some of his notable works include "Shuva" (2006), "Amar Praner Swami" (2007), and "Don Number One" (2012). Khan made his debut as a playback singer in 2011 with the film "Moner Jala." He also produced films like "Password" (2019) and "Bir" (2020). Over his career, he has received numerous awards, including four National Film Awards for best actor.

Uzlic is a long mountain in Bosnia, to the east of Maslovare-Vrbanjci-Kotor Varoš-Čelinac. It runs from southeast to northwest through hilly areas, starting from Kruševočka River (west of Borja Mountains) to Jošavka. The highest point is not specified. This mountain has many mixed forests and hunting animals, including some unique to Bosnia. Its forests are varied: oak and beech trees. It also has plenty of water sources like springs, streams, and rivers. Many smaller rivers flow from Uzlic into the Vrbanja, Usora, and Ukrina, which in turn join larger rivers like the Vrbas and the Bosna.

thixotropy means that certain gels or fluids become thinner over time when shaken. These fluids are thick and viscous when still but turn liquid-like after being agitated. They slowly return to their original state. Some, like ketchup, quickly change; others, such as yogurt, take longer. These fluids show a time-dependent change in thickness. The longer they are stressed, the thinner they get. Thixotropic materials need some time to regain their thick consistency when shaken. An example of thixotropy is that ketchup becomes liquid when shaken and returns quickly to its thick state. Yogurt, on the other hand, takes much longer to become fluid. Gels and certain mixtures can be thixotropic, staying solid until they are stirred. This happens because particles need time to rearrange themselves. Some fluids act oppositely: they get thicker when constantly stressed for a while. These are called rheopectic fluids. They are less studied than thixotropic ones.

Arjen Anthony Lucassen, born April 3, 1960, in Hilversum, Netherlands, is a Dutch musician. He performs as a singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and record producer. Best known for his long-running progressive metal/rock opera project Ayreon, he started his career as the guitarist and backup vocalist of a band called Bodine from 1980 to 1984 under the name Iron Anthony. After that, he joined another band named Vengeance until 1992. In 1995, Lucassen released an album titled "Ayreon: The Final Experiment," where he sang, wrote songs, and played most instruments. This led to the creation of Ayreon. His third album, "Into the Electric Castle," gained him more recognition as a composer of rock operas. He has been involved in many other projects including Star One, Guilt Machine, and The Gentle Storm. Lucassen also worked with Ambeon and Stream of Passion. Lucassen plays various instruments such as guitar and keyboards, and sometimes bass and banjo. In total, he has released 26 studio albums, four live albums, two EPs, and 17 singles. He has participated in over 50 albums with other artists. Since creating Ayreon, Lucassen is often praised for his creativity by rock and metal reviewers, who call him a "genius."

A disposable, also known as a disposable product, is made for one use only. After use, it's either recycled or thrown away. Sometimes, the term "disposable" is used for items that last several months (like disposable air filters) to contrast with those that can be washed and reused many times (such as washable air filters). The word "disposables" isn't the same as "consumables." In mechanical work, consumables like welding rods, tips, nozzles, and gas are replaced when they wear out. Consumables are needed for processes, such as ink for printing or rods for welding. Disposables, on the other hand, can be thrown away once they break or become unusable.
